title: 第十章　账单到期：勃列日涅夫与官名录共产主义，1964—1982
originalTitle: 10 AND THE BILL CAME DUE Brezhnev and Nomenklatura Communism, 1964-1982

children: 显然，我们已经走到了这样一个死胡同：权力的概念既不与学说相联系，也不与领袖个人相联系，也不与传统相联系，而只与权力本身相联系……
Obviously we have already reached that dead-end where the notion of power is linked neither to a doctrine, nor to the personality of a leader, nor to a tradition, but only to power as such…
自然，这样一个政权的唯一目标，至少在国内事务上，必然是自我保全……这个政权既不想恢复斯大林主义，也不想迫害知识分子的代表，也不想向那些没有请求的人提供兄弟般的援助。它只希望一切照旧：当局得到承认，知识分子闭嘴，制度不被任何危险或意外的改革所动摇。这个政权不进攻，它只自卫。它的座右铭是：别碰我们，我们也不碰你们。

Naturally the only aim of such a regime, at least in domestic affairs, must be self-preservation…. The regime neither wants to restore Stalinism, nor to persecute the representatives of the intelligentsia, nor to give fraternal aid to those who do not ask for it. It wants only that everything remains as before: that the authorities are recognized, that the intelligent-sia shuts up, and that the system not be shaken by any dangerous or unexpected reforms. The regime does not attack, it defends itself. Its motto is: don’t touch us, and we won’t touch you.
——安德烈·阿马尔里克，《苏联能存活到1984年吗？》，1969年
—Andrei Amalrik, Will the Soviet Union Survive Until 1984? 1969

zh: 赫鲁晓夫倒台后的二十年，似乎把苏联带到了其成功的顶点，带到了甚至超过斯大林1945年后所达到的国际力量水平。新领袖勃列日涅夫终于实现了赫鲁晓夫与美国取得真正核均势的抱负；他在第三世界随意干预；作为额外之举，他还用潜艇环绕各大陆。实际上，苏联此时作为超级大国屹立于世界舞台。的确，到1970年代，当西方在越南灾难、水门事件和伊朗巴列维王朝垮台的冲击下踉跄时，似乎正如苏联人惯常所说，“力量对比”正在决定性地“朝着有利于社会主义的方向”转变。诚然，东方和西方大多数人都逐渐认识到，苏联的经济表现远不如在赫鲁晓夫治下看来可能达到的那么好。尽管如此，苏联仍有可能利用其国际政治力量和不受内部危机困扰的优势，比西方更长久地存在下去，从而在“两种制度的竞赛”中胜出，或者至少成为欧亚大陆的霸主。
en: The twenty years after Khrushchev’s fall seemed to bring the Soviet Union to the apogee of its success and to a level of international power surpassing even that attained by Stalin after 1945. The new leader, Brezhnev, at last realized Khrushchev’s ambition of attaining genuine nuclear parity with the United States; he intervened at will through out the Third World; and for good measure he ringed the continents with his submarines. In truth, the Soviet Union now bestrode the world as a superpower. Indeed, by the 1970s, as the West reeled under the impact of the Vietnam disaster, Watergate, and the collapse of the shah’s Iran, it seemed as if the “correlation of forces,” as the Soviets were wont to put it, was shifting definitively “in favor of socialism.” To be sure, most people in the East and in the West progressively realized that the Soviets’ economic performance was hardly as good as it had appeared likely to become under Khrushchev. Still, the chances seemed real that the Soviet Union could use its international political strength and freedom from internal crises to outlast the West and so emerge the victor in the “competition between the two systems,” or at least the master of Eurasia.

zh: 然而实际上，这二十年是危机积聚的时期。戈尔巴乔夫后来称之为“停滞时期”，仿佛在暗示制度可以重新启动，但“衰落”和“解体”这两个词其实更为恰当。这不仅仅是因为国家由一个日益衰老、既无改革意志又无改革力量的老年领导集团统治；尽管这种衰老是问题的一部分，但它并非偶然，而是官名录制度的逻辑后果。事实上，“停滞”的更深层原因，要在苏联制度本身的基本结构中去寻找：经济、行政、意识形态、人民民主“阵营”这些结构中的每一个，都开始腐朽。1930年代和1940年代拼装起来的整套制度，到1960年代已经释放出最大潜力；而此时，就在后赫鲁晓夫领导层着手支撑它们之际，每一个制度都开始瓦解。苏联社会主义英雄时代那些代价高昂的成就，账单终于到期了。而且，从逻辑上说，列宁和斯大林创造的整个制度，正在缓慢进入总体危机。
en: In reality, however, these twenty years were a time of gathering crisis. Gorbachev later called it the “period of stagnation,” as if to imply that the system could be set moving again, but the terms “decline” and “disintegration” were really more appropriate. This was not just because the country was ruled by an increasingly decrepit gerontocracy that lacked both the will and the strength for reform; although this senescence was a part of the problem, it was no accident but a logical consequence of the

system. In fact, the deeper cause of “stagnation” was to be found in the basic structures of the Soviet system itself: Each of these structures—the economy, the administration, the ideology, the “bloc” of people’s democracies—was beginning to decay. The ensemble of institutions put together in the 1930s and 1940s had yielded its maximum potential by the 1960s, and each institution now began to decompose just as the post-Khrushchev leadership moved to prop them up. The bill for the costly successes of Soviet socialism’s heroic age was at last coming due. And, logically enough, the total system created by Lenin and Stalin was slowly entering into total crisis.

zh: 改革之火熄灭
en: REFORM FLICKERS OUT

zh: 赫鲁晓夫倒台时，看来苏联面临的唯一重大问题就是通常的继承危机。赫鲁晓夫的个人统治之后，出现了一个新的集体领导层，其模式与列宁死后苏联的两次继承相同。然而这一次，模式有了重大改变：没有出现以一位最高领袖崛起告终的权力斗争，而新领导层在本质上将保持集体领导，直到它在1980年代中期退出舞台。
en: At the time of Khrushchev’s fall, it seemed as if the only significant problem facing the Soviet Union was the usual succession crisis. Khrushchev’s personal rule was followed by a new collective leader ship in the pattern of the two Soviet successions since the death of Lenin. Yet the pattern this time was significantly modified: There was no struggle for power ending in the emergence of a supreme chief, and the new leadership would remain essentially collective until it passed from the scene in the mid-1980s.

zh: 因为赫鲁晓夫不可逆转地修改了旧的斯大林“宪法”。通过制止斯大林的恐怖，他使自己的政治局同僚免受政治警察的威胁，但他们的安全随后成了他自己脆弱性的根源：他放弃了制约党务机器的唯一手段，也就放弃了自己权力的保障。同样，他不仅给了党务官僚人身安全，还无意中给了他们终身职位。因此，当赫鲁晓夫被废黜时，官名录作为一个集体实体，成了制度的新最高首领。
en: For Khrushchev had irrevocably amended the old Stalin “constitution.” By bringing Stalin’s terror to a halt, he had made his Politburo colleagues safe from the political police, but their safety had then become the source of his own vulnerability: He had given away his only leverage against the apparat, and thus the safeguard of his own power. By the same token, he had given the apparatchiki not only physical security but also, and inadvertently, life tenure in their positions. Thus, when Khrushchev was deposed, the
as a collective entity became the new supreme chief of the system.

zh: 于是，制度中的主要职业官僚在他们自己之间分配了主要职位。赫鲁晓夫的长期门生列昂尼德·勃列日涅夫成为新的第一书记。因此，随后的十八年通常被称为“勃列日涅夫时代”；而勃列日涅夫确实可以恰当地象征他整个斯大林培养出来的一代。总理职位交给了阿列克谢·柯西金，他常被归类为“技术官僚”。但这肯定是误称，因为这位前纺织工程师在过去二十年里只做过党务机关的工作。而柯西金的经历与勃列日涅夫一代的大多数党务官僚并无不同：他们的仕途阶梯包括1930年代初至中期某种初步的“高等”技术训练，然后在清洗之后从工厂管理转入全职党务工作。有些人后来进入斯大林的中央书记处，少数人进入赫鲁晓夫的主席团。这一代人中另一位也是赫鲁晓夫门生的人，尼古拉·波德戈尔内，成为名义上的国家元首。但过于细致地区分这些人物没有意义；他们就像赫鲁晓夫手下的基里琴科和基里连科一样，或者像果戈理可能会说的，伊万·伊万诺维奇·博布钦斯基和伊万·伊万诺维奇·多布钦斯基。
en: Accordingly, leading careerists of the system divided the principal posts among themselves. Leonid Brezhnev, Khrushchev’s longtime protégé, became the new First Secretary. Thus the ensuing eighteen years are usually called “the Brezhnev era”; and Brezhnev can indeed stand as an appropriate symbol for his whole Stalin-bred generation. The post of prime minister was given to Aleksei Kosygin, who is often classified as a “technocrat.” But that is certainly a misnomer, for this former textile engineer had worked only in the Party apparat during the previous twenty years. And Kosygin’s career was not unlike that of most apparatchiki of the Brezhnev generation: Their

included a somewhat rudimentary “higher” technical training during the early to mid-1930s, and then a transfer from factory management to full-time Party work in the wake of the purges. Some went on to Stalin’s Central Committee Secretariat, and a few to Khrushchev’s Presidium. Another member of this generation who was also a protégé of Khrushchev, Nikolai Podgornyi, became the nominal head of state. But there is no point in distinguishing too finely among these figures; they are like their fellows Kirichenko and Kirilenko under Khrushchev, or, as Gogol might have said, Ivan Ivanovich Bobchinsky and Ivan Ivanovich Dobchinsky.

〔译注〕柯西金1959—1960年担任国家计委主席，1960年起任部长会议第一副主席，并非此前二十年只从事党务工作；波德戈尔内1965年才接任最高苏维埃主席团主席。

zh: 不过，有一位党务官僚值得特别一提。这就是年纪稍长的米哈伊尔·苏斯洛夫，勃列日涅夫时代的首席意识形态专家和“灰衣主教”。

他之所以有趣，是因为他的经历集中体现了苏联制度的生命周期。他出生于贫农家庭，1918年十六岁时成为村贫农委员会中的共青团积极分子。新经济政策期间，他通过工农速成班和红色经济学院一路升迁，在第一个五年计划期间成为工业学院的教授。清洗之后，他成为南方斯塔夫罗波尔省的党委书记；1944年，他主持了立陶宛的苏维埃化。1947年，这位模范的幸存者因其贡献获得中央委员会中一个隶属于日丹诺夫的职位，并由此于1952年进入斯大林的主席团。
en: Still, one apparatchik deserves special mention. This is the slightly older Mikhail Suslov, the chief ideologist and éminence grise of the Brezhnev era.

He is of interest because his career epitomizes the life cycle of the Soviet system. Born into a family of poor peasants, he became a Komsomol activist in the local committee of the village poor in 1918, at the age of sixteen. During the NEP, he worked his way up through a “Workers’ Faculty” and the Red Economics Institute to become a professor in the Industrial Institute during the First Five-Year Plan. In the wake of the purges he became Party secretary in the southern province of Stavropol; and in 1944 he supervised the Sovietization of Lithuania. In 1947 this exemplary survivor was rewarded for his services with a Central Committee post under Zhdanov, from where he moved to Stalin’s Presidium in 1952.

zh: 在赫鲁晓夫治下，为了党的改革，苏斯洛夫首先作为新领袖反对“反党集团”的主要支持者而崭露头角。随后，为了党的稳定，他又成为赫鲁晓夫过激行为的主要批评者；这促使他组织了1964年的宫廷政变。但在所有这些角色中，他始终是典型的党务工作者，这使他成为勃列日涅夫年代温和斯大林主义的主要推动者。
en: Under Khrushchev, in the interest of Party reform, Suslov first distinguished himself as the new leader’s chief supporter against the “Anti-Party Group.” Then, in the interest of Party stability, he became the chief critic of Khrushchev’s excesses; and this moved him to organize the palace coup of 1964. But in all these roles he was forever the quintessential Party man, and this led him to become the chief instigator of the soft Stalinism of the Brezhnev years.

zh: 勃列日涅夫、柯西金和苏斯洛夫的新集体领导层在宣布“干部稳定”原则时，明确表达了其纲领。这一原则很快通过废除赫鲁晓夫关于干部轮换和任期限制的党章条款而获得具体含义。恢复工作继续进行：撤销把党一分为二的做法，废除赫鲁晓夫的教育改革。接着，配合一项新的经济改革，国民经济委员会被废除，由中央部委取而代之。于是，在一年之内，赫鲁晓夫时期之前的状态被完全恢复，只有一个重大例外：没有领袖，甚至连一个像样的“老板”也没有。
en: The new collective leadership of Brezhnev, Kosygin, and Suslov made its program clear when it proclaimed the principle of “stability of cadres.” This principle was soon given concrete meaning by the abrogation of Khrushchev’s Party statutes providing for rotation of cadres in office and for time limits on tenure. The restoration continued with the recision of the Party’s division into two parts and with the suppression of Khrushchev’s educational reform. Next, in con junction with a new economic reform, the sovnarkhozes were abolished and replaced by central ministries. Thus, within a year the status quo ante Khrushchev was wholly restored but for one major exception: there was no Leader, not even much of a Boss.

zh: 在1960年代，勃列日涅夫显然只是
，即便在1970年代，尽管他在外交和国内事务中的公开地位日益突出，这一状况本质上依然如此。
他出国会见外国元首，并在缓和时期恢复了与尼克松、福特和卡特总统的峰会。在国内，1966年他做出新斯大林主义姿态，恢复总书记头衔，并把主席团改称政治局。1977年，他解除波德戈尔内的国家元首职务，自己兼任该职，正如斯大林曾经做过的那样。他让自己成为武装部队元帅，胸前挂满勋章，并出版了自己的全集（据称是理论著作）——所有这些都是苏联领袖的传统标志。然而，这些只是领袖主义（

）的装饰和外衣，反映了党国中集体领导必然倾向于产生——至少象征性地产生——一个单一首脑。事实上，他从来不像赫鲁晓夫那样是一个活跃的“老板”；实际治理依靠共识，而这一次，集体领导仍然是政治现实。因为勃列日涅夫从赫鲁晓夫倒台中很好地学到，旧口号“干部决定一切”有了新的含义：在恐怖缺席的情况下，总书记最终要对他们负责，而不是像斯大林治下那样反过来。于是，勃列日涅夫—柯西金—苏斯洛夫年代成为官名录共产主义的黄金时代。
en: In the 1960s Brezhnev was clearly only
, and this remained essentially true even in the 1970s, despite his growing public prominence in both foreign and domestic affairs.

He travelled abroad to meet with foreign heads of state, and during the period of détente he resumed summitry with Presidents Nixon, Ford, and Carter. Domestically, in 1966 he made the neo-Stalinist gestures of resuming the title General Secretary and renaming the Presidium the Politburo. In 1977 he deposed Podgornyi as president and assumed that title as well, just as Stalin had done. He made himself a marshal of the armed forces, covered his chest with medals, and published his complete (allegedly theoretical) works—all traditional attributes of a Soviet Leader. Yet these were but the trappings and the suits of

, a reflection of the inevitable tendency of collective leader ship in a Party-state to bring forth—at least symbolically—a single head. In fact, he was never as active a Boss as Khrushchev had been; government in practice was by consensus, and this time collegial leadership remained a political reality. For Brezhnev had learned very well from Khrushchev’s fall that the old slogan “cadres decide every thing” had acquired a new meaning: In the absence of terror, the General Secretary was now ultimately accountable to them, and not the other way around, as under Stalin. Thus the Brezhnev-Kosygin-Suslov years became the great age of
Communism.

zh: 于是，黑格尔“历史中的理性”观念经过一番迂回，回到了原点。对现代辩证法的创始人来说，理性的官僚阶层是引领人类实现自身目标的“普遍”阶级。马克思把这一普遍角色赋予了最受剥夺、最被非人化的阶级——无产阶级。
列宁用党取代了无产阶级，并通过宣称党是历史逻辑的表达，使由此产生的专政合法化。在勃列日涅夫“发达的”和“现实存在的”社会主义下，党的专政变成了官名录新阶级的统治。于是，普遍阶级再次成了一个自称以历史理性之名统治的官僚阶层。
en: So the peregrinations of Hegel’s idea of Reason in History had come full circle. To the founder of modern dialectics, the rational bureaucracy was the “universal” class leading mankind to its fulfillment. Marx had given this universal role to the most deprived and dehumanized class, the proletariat.

Lenin had substituted the Party for the proletariat, and he legitimated the resulting dictatorship by proclaiming it the expression of the Logic of History. Under Brezh nev’s “developed” and “really existing” socialism, the Party dictator ship became the domination of the new class of the
. Thus the universal class was once again a bureaucracy claiming to rule in the name of Reason in History.

zh: 新领导人追求稳定，绝非有意以“停滞”告终。起初他们想成为谨慎的改革者；如果他们放弃了这条路线，那是因为与赫鲁晓夫不同，他们很快从经验中得知，改革太危险，不能继续下去。他们最初的纲领分为三部分：第一，结束去斯大林化，消除知识分子异见，以恢复稳定；第二，推行较温和的经济改革路线，以保障国家的长期实力和消费者的福利；第三，以更缓慢、更少挑衅的方式寻求与美国的国际地位上的均势。因此，他们希望在不经历赫鲁晓夫方法的动荡和不确定性的情况下，追求其改革共产主义的目标。几年内他们取得了有限的进展，直到1968年布拉格之春那场大胆得多的改革共产主义把他们吓坏了，从而结束了苏联境内直到1980年代末的所有改革。
en: The new leaders by no means intended their quest for stability to end in “stagnation.” Initially they wanted to be cautious reformers; and if they abandoned this course, it was because, unlike Khrushchev, they soon learned through experience that reform was too dangerous to continue. Their initial program was in three parts: first, to end de-Stalinization and eliminate intellectual dissent in order to restore stability; second, to pursue a more moderate course of economic reform in order to provide for the country’s long-term strength and the consumer’s welfare; and third, to proceed more slowly and less provocatively with the quest for international parity with the United States. Thus, they hoped to pursue the goals of Khrushchev’s Reform Communism without the turbulence and uncertainty of his methods. And they made modest headway for a few years, until the much bolder Re form Communism of the Prague Spring of 1968 so frightened them that it ended all reform in the Soviet Union until the late 1980s.

zh: 去斯大林化的结束和对异见的攻击，以1965年逮捕两位在国外发表作品的作家安德烈·西尼亚夫斯基和尤里·丹尼尔，以及次年对他们的审判为标志。在斯大林治下，许多苏联作家当然未经公开审判便丧生，但这是第一次有人因作品内容而被定罪。两人都被判有罪，并被判处数年西伯利亚刑期，以警告所有其他人放弃萨米兹达特。但这一策略没有奏效；相反，它激起了一股规模虽小但有组织的反抗潮流。在赫鲁晓夫治下，那曾是一场混杂着愤怒与希望的反对斯大林的爆发——先是在1957年，然后在1962年——如今则变成了一场持续的运动，很快被冠以“异见”之名。
en: The end of de-Stalinization and the attack on dissidence was signalled by the arrest in 1965 of two writers who had published their texts abroad, Andrei Siniavskii and Iurii Daniel, and by their trial the following year. Under Stalin, many Soviet writers had of course perished without a public trial, but this was the first time any had been incriminated for the content of their works. Both were convicted and sentenced to several years in Siberia as a warning to all others to abandon

. But this strategem did not work; instead it sparked a small but organized current of defiance. What under Khrushchev had been an anti-Stalinist explosion mingling indignation and hope—first in 1957 and then in 1962—now became a continuing movement to which the name dissidence was soon applied.

zh: 异见运动为何在此时出现，有若干原因。赫鲁晓夫倒台不仅结束了公众对斯大林过去的探究，还引发了一场正统派反击，这场反击实际上试图为斯大林恢复名誉。的确，西尼亚夫斯基—丹尼尔审判发生在新领导层第一次党代表大会前夕，被广泛解读为积极再斯大林化的前奏。

因此，异见首先是一场针对这种可能性的自卫运动，而这一可能性直到1969年斯大林诞辰九十周年之前一直是现实的忧虑。但异见也标志着对制度可改革性的幻想日益破灭。赫鲁晓夫年代那种多少有些轻率的乐观主义，此时让位于一种认识：改革不会从上面降临，充其量只能通过漫长而缓慢的施压和斗争过程实现。不过，异见的话语此时仍然只是改革，而不是完全跳出制度。最后，异见之所以能够出现，是因为政权不再愿意诉诸过去的残酷恐怖。这并不是因为制度正在变得自由化，或正从极权主义蜕变为单纯的威权主义；这一变化是出于一个务实的原因：极端恐怖会破坏制度本身。因此，政权此时用更温和、更间接、更渐进的方法进行镇压，通常还披着“社会主义法制”的外衣，正如西尼亚夫斯基—丹尼尔审判那样。
en: There are several reasons why the dissident movement emerged at this time. Khrushchev’s fall had not only ended public probing of the Stalinist past, it had also produced an orthodox counterattack that actually sought to rehabilitate Stalin. Indeed, the Siniavskii-Daniel trial, coming on the eve of the first Party Congress of the new leadership, was widely interpreted as a prelude to active re-Stalinization.

So dissidence was in the first instance a movement of self-defense against this possibility, which remained a live concern until the ninetieth anniversary of Stalin’s birth in 1969. But dissidence was also a sign of a deepening disillusionment with the reformability of the system. The somewhat facile optimism of the Khrushchev years now gave way to the realization that reform would not fall from on high, but would at best come about through a long, slow process of pressure and struggle. Still, as yet the discourse of dissent was only of reform, not of breaking out of the system entirely. Lastly, dissidence could emerge because the regime was no longer willing to resort to the brutal terror of the past. This was not because the system was be coming liberal, or mutating from totalitarianism into mere authoritarianism; the change came about for the pragmatic reason that extreme terror was destructive of the system itself. Hence, the regime now conducted repression by softer, less direct, and more gradual methods, usually with a coating of “socialist legality,” as in the Siniavskii-Daniel trial.

zh: 因此，把勃列日涅夫时期说成新的斯大林主义是错误的。勃列日涅夫其人——即便加上苏斯洛夫——并不是斯大林；如果他在1960年代的环境下试图发动自上而下的革命和大规模恐怖，他不可能得逞。正如已经指出的，斯大林主义在共产主义制度的生命周期中只能出现一次，而那一次就是建设社会主义的关键时刻。只有那项至高任务，才能点燃真正的斯大林主义的狂热，激发其暴力。但一旦社会主义建成，政权的首要任务就变成“保卫其成果”；斯大林主义，或者更准确地说斯大林制度，便常规化并稳定为“发达社会主义”，曾经炽热的阶级斗争和战斗意识形态，变成正统咒语式的冷意识形态。
于是，苏联领导权从革命者转移到守护者手中。勃列日涅夫、柯西金和苏斯洛夫在灰色的守护之下所实行的，只是这种“温和”的斯大林主义。
en: It is therefore a mistake to talk of the Brezhnev period as a new Stalinism. Brezhnev the man—even doubled with Suslov—was no Stalin, and if he had attempted a revolution from above and mass terror, he could not have gotten away with it in the circumstances of the 1960s. As has already been noted, Stalinism can occur only once in the life cycle of a Communist regime, and that once is the pivotal moment of the building of socialism. Only that supreme task can fuel the fanaticism and stimulate the violence of real Stalinism. But once socialism is built, the primary task of the regime becomes the “defense of its conquests”; Stalinism, or more accurately the Stalin system, becomes routinized and stabilized as “developed socialism,” The once hot ideology of class struggle and combat becomes a cold ideology of orthodox incantation.
And consequently Soviet leader ship passes from the revolutionaries to the guardians. It is only this “soft” Stalinism that was practiced under the gray guardianship of Brezhnev, Kosygin, and Suslov.

zh: 他们的极权主义之所以较为温和，另一个原因是经济状况。经济此时过于庞大和复杂，无法用1930年代的残酷方法来管理，甚至也无法承受战后重建时期的那种紧缩。此外，已经不可能再推迟某种程度的消费满足，而这意味着农业的表现必须改善。赫鲁晓夫在这方面已经指明了道路，没有回头路可走。事实上，新领导层觉得，为了制度的稳定和作为超级大国的军事力量的发展，有必要在赫鲁晓夫的经济成绩上更进一步。因此，在经济方面，起初没有重新冻结，反而进一步推进了改革。
en: Another reason why their totalitarianism was more muted was the state of the economy. It was now too huge and too complex to be run with the brutal methods employed in the 1930s, or even with the stringencies imposed during the postwar reconstruction. Moreover, it was no longer possible to defer some measure of consumer satisfaction, and that meant the performance of agriculture had to be improved. Khrushchev had already shown the way on this score, and there was no going back. Indeed, the new leadership felt it was necessary to improve on Khrushchev’s economic record in the interests of both the system’s stability and the development of its military strength as a superpower. In economics, therefore, there was at first no refreeze, but rather an extension of the reform effort.

zh: 这在农业方面尤其明显。尽管赫鲁晓夫不安分的“运动”被叫停，但他最重要的纲领得到加强。对化学工业的投资扩大了，化肥产量增加了。向集体农庄庄员支付的粮食和牲畜价格提高了。对自留地的限制放宽了。最重要的是，在勃列日涅夫年代，农业投资大幅增加；它最终占预算的四分之一，当时苏联投入农业的国家资源比例超过任何其他国家。曾经被忽视的农村，终于成为政权的最高优先事项。生产确实显著改善，速度甚至快于大多数西方国家。
尽管如此，农业仍然是一个危机领域：每一次歉收都是一场全国性的危机，国家经常不得不进口粮食，尤其是为了饲养牲畜。
en: This was especially marked in agriculture. Although Khrushchev’s restless “campaigning” was called off, his most important programs were intensified. Investment in the chemical industry was expanded, and the production of artificial fertilizers was increased. Prices paid to kolkhozniks for grain and livestock were raised. Restrictions on the private plot were eased. Above all, during the Brezhnev years investment in agriculture increased enormously; it eventually accounted for a quarter of the budget, at which time the Soviet Union was devoting a greater proportion of national resources to agriculture than any other country. The once neglected countryside had at long last become a top priority of the regime. And production did improve notably, in deed at a faster rate than in most Western countries.
All the same, agriculture remained a crisis area: each bad harvest was a national drama, and the country regularly had to import grain, especially to feed its livestock.

zh: 这种相对失败的一个原因，是苏联农业此前太过低迷，即使快速增长也无法大幅提高生产水平。此外，城市和农村人口收入都上升了，需求因此显著增加。而且，很大一部分人口仍从事农业，这造成低生产率并推高总成本：苏联城市人口直到1961年才首次超过农村人口，而农村人口在1985年仍占总人口的30%。即便如此，收获季节总是缺乏劳动力，数百万城市居民和士兵不得不被动员去收割庄稼。
en: One reason for this relative failure was that Soviet agriculture had been so depressed that even rapid growth could not raise the level of production very much. In addition, the incomes of both the urban and the rural populations had risen, and demand had therefore significantly increased. Moreover, a large proportion of the population still worked in agriculture, thus making for a low level of productivity and increasing overall costs: The Soviet Union’s urban population surpassed the rural population for the first time only in 1961, and the latter still accounted for 30 percent of the total population in 1985. Even so, there was always a shortage of labor at harvest time, and millions of city dwellers and soldiers had to be mobilized to bring in the crops.

zh: 显然，农业失败的基本原因是组织性的：整个事业——巨额投资、化肥的普遍使用、收获运动——仍然由上面和中央管理。因此，政权继续推行把集体农庄转变为国营农场的政策，到1980年代，国营农场占全国耕地面积的一半以上。与此同时，少数胆怯却相当成功的“小组制度”实验，被职业化的集体农庄管理者压制了。简而言之，政权进一步强化了惯常的命令—行政方法，得到了惯常的适得其反的结果，却不可能提倡任何其他政策。
en: It is clear that the basic cause of the agricultural failure was organizational: The whole enterprise—the massive investments, the generalized use of chemical fertilizers, the harvest campaigns—continued to be managed from above and from the center. Thus, the regime pressed on with its policy of transforming kolkhozes into sovkhozes, and by the 1980s the latter accounted for more than half of the cultivated area of the country. At the same time, the few timid yet quite successful experiments conducted with the “link system” were sup pressed by the professional kolkhoz managers. In short, the regime had amplified the usual command-administrative methods and obtained the usual counterproductive results, yet it was impossible to advocate any other policy.

zh: 因此，到勃列日涅夫时代末期，粮食供应相对于需求正在下降；而农业在斯大林治下曾是（强制）积累资本、为工业投资提供资金的来源，此时却成了经济其他部分的净负担。
此时已经清楚，即使颠倒经典的斯大林主义经济优先次序，集体化农业也无法变得有生产力；而这种僵局的代价只能削弱整个制度。由此造成的贫困化，就是列宁革命性“结合”（
）中次要伙伴——工农联盟中的农民——的最终命运。
en: Consequently, by the end of the Brezhnev era the food supply was declining in relation to demand; and agriculture, which under Stalin had been a source of (forced) accumulation of capital for investment in industry, had become a net burden on the rest of the economy.

It was now clear that even with a reversal of the classic Stalinist economic priorities, collectivized agriculture could not be made productive; and the cost of this impasse could only undermine the system as a whole. The resulting impoverishment was the final fate of the junior partner in Lenin’s revolutionary
, the alliance of workers and peasants.

zh: “结合”中的主要伙伴——工人——在勃列日涅夫治下也陷入了类似的僵局，整个工业部门也遭遇了同样的困境。这里的转折点是1965年柯西金经济改革的失败。但这不仅仅是勃列日涅夫主义的又一个黯淡插曲，因为它标志着整个改革共产主义事业的核心纲领的失败。
en: The senior partner in the

, the workers, reached a similar impasse under Brezhnev, as did the whole industrial sector. Here the turning point was the failure of the Kosygin economic reform of 1965. But this was more than just another dismal episode of Brezhnevism, for it marked the defeat of the central program of the entire Reform Communist enterprise.

zh: 集中化经济中的经济改革只能朝一个方向走——走向分权化和市场。的确，自斯大林在1930年代建立命令经济以来，所有改革努力都朝这个方向。第一次胆怯地暗示要朝这个方向前进，出现在二战后关于“小组制度”的讨论中。一个共产党政府公开承认分权化可能是改革目标，是在1950年代初铁托宣布其“自我管理”政策时，随后又是在1957年他提出纲领草案时。这一方向在老市场社会主义者奥斯卡·兰格手中获得了理论上的精致化；1945年他回到波兰参与在家乡建设社会主义时受到冷遇，但在1956年波兰十月期间取得了较好的结果。而赫鲁晓夫的解冻把这一思想路线带入了俄国的讨论：1960年代，俄国学院经济学的传统——它曾在1920年代是世界上最富创造力的传统之一——开始胆怯地复兴，不仅作为一门理论和数学学科，也作为一个具有实际意义的思潮。
en: Economic reform in a centralized economy can take only one direction—towards decentralization and the market. Indeed, this had been the direction taken by all reform efforts since Stalin created the command economy in the 1930s. The first, timid intimations of moving in such a direction came during discussions of the “link system” after the Second World War. The open acknowledgment by a Communist government that decentralization might be the objective of reform’ came when Tito proclaimed his policy of “self-management” in the early 1950s, and then when he introduced his Draft Program in 1957. This direction received theoretical sophistication at the hands of the old market-socialist Oskar Lange, who had been ignored when he returned to Poland in 1945 to participate in building socialism in his homeland, but who met with better results during the Polish October of 1956. And Khrushchev’s thaw brought this line of thought into the discussion in Russia: in the 1960s the Russian tradition of academic economics, which had been one of the most creative in the world in the 1920s, began to timidly revive, not only as a theoretical and mathematical discipline, but also as a school of thought with practical implications.

zh: 这些实际主张最早在1962年由叶夫谢·利伯曼教授的一篇文章阐明，文章以《计划、利润、奖金》为题发表在《真理报》上。很快被称为“利伯曼主义”的主张，要求给予企业更大自主权，允许它们为利润而经营，这反过来将提供投资资本以及对工人和管理人员的物质激励。此外，由于工业要按列宁的
）即盈亏原则运作，企业将被允许破产。如果实施，利伯曼主义将把斯大林主义制度颠倒过来：生产目标不会只用数量和吨位的实物单位表示，还会考虑质量和成本；管理决策不会由上级下达，而是对供求的市场力量作出反应。“社会主义竞赛”、“突击工作”和“斯达汉诺夫运动”的伪竞争手法和道德—意识形态激励，将被不那么社会主义但更有效的利润和收益激励所取代。
en: These implications were first spelled out in 1962 in an article by Professor Yevsei Liberman that appeared in

under the title “Plan, Profit, Premium.” What quickly became known as “Libermanism” advocated according greater autonomy to enterprises and permitting them to work for a profit, which in turn would provide investment capital as well as material incentives for labor and management. Moreover, since industry was to operate on the basis of Lenin’s

, or profit and loss, enterprises would be allowed to go bankrupt. If implemented, Libermanism would have turned the Stalinist system on its head: production goals would not have been expressed only in physical units of quantity and tonnage, but would also have taken into account quality and cost; and management decisions would not have been commanded from above, but would have come as responses to the market forces of supply and demand. The pseudocompetitive techniques and moral-ideological incentives of “socialist emulation,” “shock work,” and “Stakhanovism” would have been replaced by the less socialist but more effective incentives of profit and gain.

zh: 这些想法得到了复兴中的苏联经济学的主要代表人物——V. S. 涅姆钦诺夫、L. V. 康托罗维奇和V. V. 诺沃日洛夫——的支持。事实上，他们把利伯曼主义大大向前推进：他们主张按照更理性和科学的方向重组经济，引入此前被谴责为“资产阶级”的控制论和系统分析的洞见，并使计划计算机化以增加其灵活性。他们甚至暗示，这些变化将需要对党国进行改革。
en: These ideas received the support of the major representatives of the renascent discipline of Soviet economics—V. C. Nemchinov, L. V. Kantorovich, and V. V. Novozhilov. Indeed, they developed Libermanism much further: they advocated reorganizing the economy on more rational and scientific lines by introducing the insights of cybernetics and systems analysis (hitherto denounced as “bourgeois”), and by computerizing the Plan to make it more flexible. And they even intimated that these changes would require reform of the Party-state.

children: 〔译注〕该经济学家的俄文全名为瓦西里·谢尔盖耶维奇·涅姆钦诺夫，其拉丁字母姓名缩写通常作 V. S.，原书作 V. C.。
〔译注〕该经济学家的俄文全名为瓦西里·谢尔盖耶维奇·涅姆钦诺夫，其拉丁字母姓名缩写通常作 V. S.，原书作 V. C.。

zh: 赫鲁晓夫及其同僚对这种新思想感兴趣，尽管他们当然没有意识到它对制度的颠覆潜力。事实上，正是赫鲁晓夫支持发表利伯曼的文章，而且就在他倒台前不久，他还把后者的方法引入两家纺织厂。赫鲁晓夫被废黜两天后，柯西金把实验扩展到其他企业，取得了相当大的成功。次年，另一位改革派经济学家阿贝尔·阿甘别吉扬（他后来在戈尔巴乔夫治下发挥重要作用）向中央委员会发出警报。在一份机密报告中，他详细说明了苏联经济相对于美国的衰退，并把这种衰退归因于过度集中化和过重的国防负担。
正是为了阻止这种衰退、同时维持国防体系，柯西金发动了1965年的改革。
en: Khrushchev and his colleagues were interested in this new thinking, though they certainly did not realize its subversive potential for the system. Indeed, it was Khrushchev who had sponsored Liberman’s article, and, just before his fall, he introduced the latter’s methods into two textile factories. Two days after Khrushchev was deposed, Kosygin extended the experiment to other enterprises, where it met with considerable success. The next year another reform economist, Abel Aganbegyan (who would later play a significant role under Gorbachev), sounded the alarm to the Central Committee. In a confidential report, he detailed the decline of the Soviet economy relative to that of the United States and attributed this decline to overcentralization and an inordinate defense burden.
It was to arrest this decline yet at the same time maintain the defense establishment that Kosygin launched his 1965 reform.

zh: 如前所述，这项改革的第一步是废除国民经济委员会，由中央部委取而代之。第二步是扩大企业的管理自主权，企业因此应当按盈利原则运作。企业此时从各自的部委收到数量减少的具体目标，即“指标”（从四十个减为八个），销售量取代总产值成为成功的主要标准。与此同时，物质激励——以支付给管理层和工人的奖金或额外报酬的形式——通过一个复杂的制度与利润挂钩。然而，企业不能根据需求或社会需要自行定价；价格由一个名为国家价格委员会的新组织按照旧标准确定，即满足由计划而非市场决定的“需要”。但没有自行定价的自由，企业的盈利能力就成了其成功的边缘性标准。此外，也也没有提供足够资金来增加工人的奖金激励。同样，回到中央部委也往往抵消了企业的新自主权。
en: The first step in this reform, as noted earlier, was to abolish the sovnarkhozes and to replace them by central ministries. The second step was to expand the managerial autonomy of enterprises, which were accordingly supposed to operate on the basis of profitability. Enterprises now received from their ministries a reduced number of specific targets, or “indicators” (eight instead of forty), and sales volume replaced gross output as the principal criterion of success. At the same time, material incentives—in the form of bonuses or premiums paid to both management and workers—were linked to profits by a complicated system. Yet enterprises could not set their own prices in accordance with demand or social need; prices were set by a new organization, Goskomtsen, according to the old criteria of meeting “needs” determined by the Plan, not by the market. But without the freedom to charge their own prices, the enterprises’ profitability became a marginal criterion of their success. In addition, funds were not forthcoming to provide increased bonuses as incentive to the workers. Similarly, the return to central ministries tended to negate the new autonomy of the enterprises.

zh: 这些内在矛盾是改革在1968年后停滞的原因之一。另一个原因是同年的布拉格之春，那是迄今最重大的改革共产主义实验（后文将详述）。它的主要特征之一，是一场与柯西金改革相似但更大胆的经济改革。而苏联人从捷克改革中吸取的教训之一是，经济自由化太容易升级为政治自由化，从而威胁政权的根本基础。因此，捷克经验在各层苏联官员中引发了极大恐慌：在最高层，柯西金被劝阻不要推进其纲领；下层党务官僚则自发削减改革措施。
en: These built-in contradictions were one reason the reform ground to a halt after 1968. Another was the Prague Spring of that same year, the most substantial experiment in Reform Communism ever attempted (but more on this later). One of its principal features was an economic reform similar to, but bolder than, Kosygin’s. And one of the lessons the Soviets drew from the Czech reform was that economic liberalization could all too easily escalate into political liberalization that would threaten the very foundations of the regime. Thus the Czech experience threw a great scare into Soviet officials at all levels: at the top, Kosygin was discouraged from pressing his program, and lower apparatchiki spontaneously cut it back.

zh: 但即使没有布拉格之春，制度的结构也注定柯西金的纲领失败。管理者利用自主权去完成计划目标，而不是冒险进行生产创新；部委则也乐于相应调整指标；而两者都在斯大林主义经济的命令文化中成长起来，宁愿固守熟悉的常规。于是，一场官僚之间无声的合谋慢慢掏空了改革，生产继续下降，质量继续恶化。但与此同时，官僚机构却扩张了：国家计划委员会和国家价格委员会之外，又增加了国家物资技术供应委员会（Gosnab）和国家科学技术委员会（GKNT），而工业部委的数量从1965年的四十五个增加到1985年的七十多个。
en: But even in the absence of a Prague Spring, the structure of the system doomed Kosygin’s program to failure. Managers used their autonomy to meet the targets of the Plan rather than to risk innovations in production; ministries were only too willing to adjust the indicators accordingly; and both, having been raised in the command culture of Stalinist economics, preferred to stick to familiar routines. Thus a silent conspiracy of bureaucrats slowly eviscerated the reform, and production continued to decline and quality to deteriorate. But at the same time, the bureaucracy expanded: Gosplan and Goskomtsen were joined by Gosnab (in charge of material-technical supply) and GKNT (in charge of scientific and technological inputs), while the number of industrial ministries increased from forty-five in 1965 to more than seventy in 1985.

zh: 然而，尽管苏联工业生产体系及其官僚上层建筑同时扩张，国民产品和工人生产率的增长率却继续下降。虽然确切数字存在争议，但总趋势没有争议。
en: Yet despite the concurrent expansion of the Soviet industrial plant and its bureaucratic superstructure, the rates of growth of both national product and worker productivity continued to decline. Although the exact figures are in dispute, the general trend is not.

zh: 当时，世界不得不在苏联官方数字和中央情报局（CIA）略低的估计之间选择，而且即便在许多苏联经济学家当中，也普遍认为后者更接近真相。然而到1980年代末，情况已经清楚：中央情报局的数字只是比苏联官方数字虚高得略少一些。中央情报局的估计之所以偏差如此之大，有两个原因：第一，中央情报局不得不使用的苏联统计数据往往被“做假”过，为了完成计划和获得奖金而夸大成绩；第二，甚至更重要的是，西方评估苏联国民生产总值（GNP）的方法——苏联人自己并不使用这种衡量方式——存在根本缺陷。
en: At the time, the world had to choose between the official Soviet figures and the somewhat lower estimates of the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), and there was a general consensus, even among many Soviet economists, that the latter were closer to the truth. By the late 1980s, however, it became clear that the CIA figures were only some what less inflated than the official Soviet ones. There are two reasons why the CIA’s estimates were so far off the mark: first, the Soviet statistics the CIA had to work with were often “cooked” to exaggerate performance for the benefit of the Plan and for the purpose of obtaining bonuses; and second, and even more important, the Western method of evaluating Soviet gross national product (GNP)—a measurement not used by the Soviets themselves—was fundamentally flawed.

zh: 缺陷在于命令经济与市场经济不可通约，因而也在于比较两种经济表现的方法。与流行看法相反，国民生产总值不是一个事实，而是一个概念；更确切地说，它是一种测量，而没有理论前提就不可能有测量。因此，对苏联国民生产总值规模的任何估计，都反映了它所依据的理论。而主要问题恰恰出在理论领域。我们关于经济产出的一切理论都源自西方的经验和数据，而主要数据是价格。但苏联的价格没有经济逻辑；它们的“逻辑”是政治逻辑或“指令”逻辑——是计划的逻辑，而不是市场的逻辑。因此，需要一个“成本调整系数”，才能把苏联的“价格”转换成可以输入西方先进计量经济学测量模型的数据。
en: The flaw lay in the incommensurability of a command economy and a market economy, and therefore in the techniques for comparing performance in the one with performance in the other. Contrary to widespread opinion, GNP is not a fact but a concept; more precisely, it is a measurement, and there can be no measurement without the oretical premises. Thus any estimate of the size of the Soviet GNP is a reflection of the theory upon which it is based. And it is here, in the realm of theory, that a major problem arises. All of our theories concerning economic output are derived from Western experience and data, and the principal data are prices. But Soviet prices have no economic logic; their “logic” is a political or a “command” logic—the logic of the Plan, not of the market. Hence, a “cost adjustment factor” is required to convert Soviet “prices” into data that can be fed into the measurement models of advanced Western econometrics.

zh: 这些模型主要是在1930年代和1940年代在英美两地的剑桥发展出来的，本来是为了处理大萧条造成的问题。后来在1960年代，它们被改造用于以据说冷静而科学的学术方式分析对手苏联制度，此后又被中央情报局用来监测这个对手在冷战几十年间的演变。
en: These models, developed largely in the two Cambridges in the 1930s and 1940s, were meant to handle the problems created by the Great Depression. They were then transmogrified in the 1960s for the purpose of analyzing the rival Soviet system in putatively sober and scientific academic fashion, and thereafter they were used by the CIA to monitor the rival’s evolution through the decades of the Cold War.

zh: 到1970年代，中央情报局关于苏联经济规模约为美国60%的估计已被普遍接受；这个数字既可以被解释为威胁的标志，也可以被解释为希望的标志，取决于观点。中央情报局的评估，以及更早、甚至更为乐观的估计，受到流亡的苏联经济学家的全面批评（如1950年代和1960年代的瑙姆·亚斯尼，以及1980年代的伊戈尔·比尔曼）。这些经济学家认为，苏联统计是政治的，不是经济的；计划由于不考虑成本，对资本极其浪费；西方的估计被严重夸大，因为它们没有考虑整个苏联国民产品的低质量。
当时，这些批评者通常被斥为心怀怨愤的流亡者。但当公开性最终允许苏联经济学家——例如尼古拉·什梅廖夫、加夫里尔·波波夫、斯坦尼斯拉夫·沙塔林和叶戈尔·盖达尔——在1980年代末公开发言时，他们充分证实了流亡同胞对中央情报局和西方学术界估计的悲观、或者更准确地说现实的裁决。事实上，这些俄罗斯经济学家现在建议把中央情报局的数字降低约2%，以获得大致接近真相的概念。
en: By the 1970s the CIA’s estimate that the size of the Soviet economy was some 60 percent of the American was generally accepted; this was a figure that could be construed as the indicator of a threat or of a promise, depending upon one’s point of view. The CIA’s evaluation, as well as earlier and even more optimistic estimates, was roundly criticized by émigré Soviet economists (such as Naum Jasny in the 1950s and 1960s, and Igor Birman in the 1980s) on several grounds. These economists argued that Soviet statistics were political, not economic; that the Plan, because it did not take account of costs, was inordinately wasteful of capital; and that Western estimates were grossly inflated because they did not take into consideration the low quality of the entire Soviet national product.
At the time, these critics were generally dismissed as sour émigrés. But when

at last permitted Soviet economists—for example, Nikolai Shmelev, Gavriil Popov, Stanislav Shatalin, and Yegor Gaidar—to speak out in the late eighties, they amply confirmed the pessimistic, or more accurately realistic, verdict of their émigré compatriots on the estimates of the CIA and Western academia. In fact, these Russian economists now advise reducing the CIA’s figures by about 2 percent to get an approximate idea of the truth.

zh: 那么，我们现在能给勃列日涅夫时期、或者斯大林在1930年代与“资产阶级”统计学决裂之后的苏联经济表现给出什么数字呢？我们仍然不知道，而且大概永远不会知道，因为苏联政治经济学的超现实运作，按其本性就无法转换成“正常的”经济术语。这样一种“经济”没有产生真正的统计，正如它没有采用真正的价格一样，并非偶然：它的簿记是计划的政治会计；而计划是由意识形态意志驱动的，不是由盈亏机制的驱动驱动的，无论政权曾如何劝诫其经理们服从经济核算的纪律——无论在列宁、柯西金还是戈尔巴乔夫时代。
en: So what figures can we now put on the Soviet economic performance under Brezhnev, or under Stalin in the 1930s, after he broke with “bourgeois” statistics? We still do not know, and we probably never will, for the surreal operations of the Soviet political economy by their very nature cannot be translated into “normal” economic terms. It is no more of an accident that such an “economy” did not generate real statistics than that it did not employ real prices: its bookkeeping was the political accounting of the Plan; and the Plan was driven by ideological will, not by the goad of profit and loss, however much the regime may have exhorted its managers to submit to the discipline of
, whether in the days of Lenin, Kosygin, or Gorbachev.

zh: 不过，中央情报局的旧数字仍能粗略指示趋势，而趋势是稳步向下的。
en: Still, the old CIA figures can give a rough indication of trend, and the trend is steadily downward.

zh: 因此，按照俄罗斯经济学家建议的适当扣减两个百分点，到1979—1980年，苏联很可能已经进入负增长区间。
en: Thus, with the appropriate deduction of 2 percent suggested by the Russian economists, by 1979-1980 the Soviet Union had probably entered the zone of negative-growth.

〔译注〕前表的1976—1980年平均增长率为2.3%，即使减去两个百分点仍为0.3%；这一整段时期的均值本身不能证明1979—1980年为负增长，结论还取决于具体年份和估计方法。

zh: 但问题还不止于此。更具威胁性的是，苏联经济在1960年代和1970年代错过了其他工业社会更早完成的从粗放发展向集约发展的重大转折。1930年代、1940年代甚至1950年代苏联经济的巨大成功，是靠制度化战争经济的方法取得的，这种方法把大量人力和资本投入大型项目。它还以肆意的浪费挥霍这些资源——古拉格只是最恶劣的例子。这种挥霍之所以可能，首先是因为19世纪末20世纪初的人口大爆炸使俄国成为欧洲人口最多的国家；因此，苏联实验拥有一个人口储备，斯大林粗放的发展方法，尤其是他的恐怖饥荒，可以不加算计地从中汲取。斯大林的资源挥霍之所以可能，其次是因为该国广阔的欧亚疆域——苏联政府不断吹嘘的世界陆地面积的六分之一——提供或似乎提供了取之不尽的原料储备：生荒地可以不顾土壤侵蚀地开垦，河流可以为了伪普罗米修斯式的工程项目而筑坝或改道。
en: But this was not all that was wrong. Even more threatening was the fact that the Soviet economy in the 1960s and 1970s missed the great turn from extensive to intensive development that other industrialized societies had made earlier. The great Soviet economic successes of the 1930s, the 1940s, and even the 1950s had been achieved by the methods of an institutionalized war economy that used great quantities of men and capital in large-scale projects. It had also expended these resources with wanton wastefulness—the Gulag was only the worst example. Such extravagance had been possible, first, because the great population explosion of the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries had made Russia by far the most populous nation in Europe; hence the Soviet experiment had a demographic reservoir on which Stalin’s extensive methods of development, in particular his terror famine, could draw without counting. Stalin’s extravagant use of resources had been possible, second, because the country’s vast Eur asian expanse—one sixth of the world’s land surface, as the Soviet government constantly boasted—offered, or seemed to offer, inexhaustible reserves of raw materials: virgin lands could be plowed with out heed to soil erosion, and rivers could be dammed or diverted in pseudo-Promethean engineering projects.

zh: 但到1970年代，该国的人力和自然资源都已严重枯竭。
斯大林对农民阶层的摧残之后，苏联城市长期住房短缺，迫使城市家庭大幅限制子女数量；国家的劳动力相应萎缩，尤其是在斯拉夫核心地带。与此同时，布尔什维克工业化的“风暴与征服”方法开始耗尽曾经丰富的物质储备，取而代之的是生态灾难区，如不断缩小的咸海和濒死的贝加尔湖。劳动力减少和自然资源枯竭，使一切经济活动都变得更加昂贵。
en: But by the 1970s both the human and natural resources of the country had become seriously depleted.

After the decimation of the peasantry under Stalin, the chronic housing shortage in the Soviet cities led urban families to restrict their size drastically; the country’s labor force shrank correspondingly, especially in the Slavic heartland. At the same time, the “storm and conquer” methods of Bolshevik industrialization were beginning to exhaust once abundant material reserves, and in their place ecological disaster areas had appeared, such as the shrinking Aral Sea and the dying Lake Baikal. And the decline of the labor force and the depletion of natural resources made all economic operations more costly.

〔译注〕据国际组织的苏联经济研究，全苏劳动年龄人口在1970年代仍在增长，1980年代增速才明显放缓；这与本段将整个1970年代劳动力描述为绝对萎缩的说法并不一致。

zh: 显然，转变的时候已经到了：应当从适合建设社会主义英雄时代的粗放发展方法，转向适合真正成熟工业体系的更集约的方法——以节约稀缺资源、培养人的技能和更精细的技术为基础的方法。政权的一些领导人，如柯西金本人以及后来的安德罗波夫，也意识到了这一点。柯西金最初主张以“科学”和“理性”的管理方法，而不是突击式的“运动”，作为进一步增长的关键；后来政权声称自己正在进行一场“科学技术革命”。但这一切都无济于事。
en: The time had clearly come for a transition from the extensive methods of development adequate for the Homeric age of building socialism to the more intensive methods appropriate to a genuinely mature industrial system—methods based on the husbanding of scarce resources, the cultivation of human skills, and a more refined technology. And some leaders of the regime, such as Kosygin himself and later Andropov, were aware of this. Kosygin initially advocated “scientific” and “rational” methods of management, rather than crash “campaigns,” as the key to further growth; and later the regime claimed it was engaged in a “scientific-technological revolution.” But all to no avail.

zh: 到1970年代和1980年代，苏联与西方的技术差距不断扩大；更不祥的是，差距扩大的速度逐年加快。
苏联经济中唯一没有丧失竞争力的部门是军事部门，但如果体系其余部分日益过时，它也无法长期保持地位。然而，向集约方法的转变，恰恰是中央计划体制事实证明完全无法完成的。
en: By the 1970s and 1980s the technological gap between the Soviet Union and the West was growing; even more ominous was the fact that the rate at which the gap was widening was increasing by the year.

The only sector of the Soviet economy that was not declining in competitive capacity was the military, but even it could not maintain its position for long if the rest of the system was becoming obsolete. Yet the transition to intensive methods was one that the central Plan proved quite unable to make.

zh: 换一种说法来表述这个制度的长期困境：1930年代，苏联人建造了一个粗糙但可用的匹兹堡—底特律或鲁尔—洛林式经济体，并主要将其用于军事目的。战后，他们重建了这套工业体系——此时它已不再处于世界工业实践的前沿——并给它加上了核武器和弹道导弹发展的新使命。最后，在斯大林死后，他们把这一模式数倍扩展，而与此同时，更先进的国家正在淘汰自己的加里、伯明翰和埃森，转而利用韩国等廉价优质钢材来源；而在高度发达的国家，技术前沿已经推进到硅谷。
en: To put the long-term dilemma of the system another way, in the 1930s the Soviets had built a crude but serviceable version of a Pittsburgh-Detroit or a Ruhr-Lorraine economy, and directed it primarily towards military uses. After the war they rebuilt this plant—when it was no longer at the avant-garde of world industrial practices—and imposed on it the new mission of nuclear and ballistic development. Finally, after Stalin’s death, they multiplied this model several times over while more advanced countries were phasing out their Garys, Birminghams, and Essens, and utilizing instead such sources of cheap high-quality steel as South Korea; and back in the highly developed countries, the technological frontier moved on to Silicon Valley.

zh: 诚然，苏联人确实在核技术上与利弗莫尔和洛斯阿拉莫斯并驾齐驱。但在其他方面，西方和东亚以塑料与化学、电子、家用耐用品、最后是计算机世界的革命向他们提出挑战——这些挑战，苏联人只能笨拙地纳入计划体制这台利维坦机器。与此同时，苏联商品（军用品除外）的质量稳步恶化，国家基础设施和资本存量也是如此，从铁路到工厂到住房；到1980年代，该国大部分地区简直在化为废墟。而这种从停滞到恶化的下降，是计划逻辑在达到一定工业发展水平后的直接结果。因为归根结底，计划不仅意味着静态的供求水平，还意味着静态的技术，而这样的条件在现实世界中永远不可能存在。在动态的现实世界里，事物要么上升，要么下降，但绝不会静止不动。然而整个苏联制度的前提，是达到“社会主义”然后停留在那里，仿佛那就是历史的终结。
en: To be sure, the Soviets did match Livermore and Los Alamos. But for the rest, the West and East Asia challenged them with revolutions in plastics and chemicals, then in electronics, then in household durables, and finally in the world of computers—challenges that the Soviets could only clumsily incorporate into the Leviathan machinery of the Plan. At the same time, the quality of Soviet goods (except those for the military) steadily deteriorated, as did the national infra structure and the capital stock, from railroads to factories to housing; by the 1980s much of the country was literally crumbling into ruin. And this descent from stagnation to deterioration was a direct result of the logic of the Plan once a certain level of industrial development had been achieved. For in the final analysis, planning implies not only a static level of supply and demand but also a static technology, and such conditions can never exist in the real world. In the dynamic world of reality things either go up or they go down, but they never remain stationary. Yet the whole Soviet system was predicated on attaining “socialism” and then staying there, as if that were the end of history.

zh: 衰退的另一个原因，是那个本应是苏联制度社会基础、本应为之而存在的群体——工人阶级——的悲惨状况。它的处境之所以格外关键，是因为在勃列日涅夫年代，工人第一次成为苏联人口的多数。1929年工业化开始时，工人阶级只比1917年略大，即约占人口的2%到3%。即使在1930年代末，即革命城市化的十年结束时，农民仍占人口的66%。直到1961年，城市人口才超过农村人口。这一平衡在勃列日涅夫治下继续转变；到1982年，约70%的苏联人是城市居民，其中大多数当然是工人。正是这个不断扩大的城市人口的压力，迫使赫鲁晓夫和勃列日涅夫政权把越来越多的资源用于消费需求和农业改善。
en: Another cause of the decline was the sorry condition of the group that was supposed to be the Soviet system’s social base, and for whose welfare that system was supposed to exist, the working class. Its plight was all the more central because during the Brezhnev years workers for the first time became the majority of the Soviet population. In 1929, at the beginning of industrialization, the working class was only slightly larger than in 1917, that is, around 2 or 3 percent of the population. Even at the end of the 1930s, the decade of revolutionary urbanization, peasants still accounted for 66 percent of the population. It was only in 1961 that the urban population surpassed the rural population. The balance continued to shift under Brezhnev; by 1982 some 70 percent of the Soviet people were urban dwellers, and of course the majority of these were workers. And it was the pressure of this constantly expanding urban population that forced the regimes of Khrushchev and Brezhnev to devote ever more resources to consumer needs and the improvement of agriculture.

zh: 当然，政权从未停止宣称工人在制度中至高无上，他的“社会主义劳动”是制度力量的源泉。作为对人民牺牲的一种伪正当化，工人国家神话确实是制度运作的核心。这个神话无疑是社会主义建设突击阶段一种有力的心理动员手段，而且很明显，工人阶级的一部分人为其成员中的精英所获得的威望感到自豪。然而，要让这一神话在普通工人中继续生效，就必须先让他们从“光辉未来”中得到更实在的好处，而这从未充分兑现。
en: The regime, of course, never ceased to proclaim that the worker was supreme in the system and that his “socialist labor” was the source of the system’s strength. As a pseudo-legitimation of the sacrifices of the population, the myth of the workers’ state was indeed central to the functioning of the system. This myth was undoubtedly a potent means of psychological mobilization during the crash phases of building socialism, and it is clear that a part of the working class took pride in the prestige accorded to an elite among its members. Nonetheless, a more tangible down payment on the “radiant future” was necessary for the rank and file to keep the myth alive, and this was never adequately forthcoming.

zh: 正如我们已经看到的，斯大林1931年放弃早期布尔什维主义的平等主义政策后，劳动力受到两种手段的驱动：对少数斯达汉诺夫式成就者的特殊奖励，以及对普通群众的计件工资压力。在这十年中，这些措施之外又加上了劳动手册、居住证（propiska）的警察压力，以及对旷工的刑事处罚；最后，1940年，政权诉诸于把劳动者固定在工作岗位上的强制措施。这套严酷制度在战后有所缓和；特别是刑事处罚的使用减少了，对城市工人最需要的商品降价，因为斯大林偏爱他们胜过其他社会群体。尽管如此，当时的普遍贫困使工人只能享受最基础的社会服务，计件工资仍是常态。
en: As we have seen, once the egalitarian policies of early Bolshevism were abandoned by Stalin in 1931, the labor force was driven by a combination of special rewards for the few Stakhanovite achievers and the pressure of piece-rates for the rank and file. To these measures were added, in the course of the decade, the police pressure of the labor book, the

(residence permit), and criminal penalties for absenteeism; finally, in 1940, the regime resorted to labor mobilization on the job. This draconian regimen was softened after the war; in particular, the use of criminal penalties was reduced, and prices were decreased on goods that benefited urban workers most, for Stalin had a preference for them over other social groups. Still, the general poverty of the times was such that the workers enjoyed only the most rudimentary social services, and piece-rates remained the norm.

zh: 斯大林死后的放松时期，向工人让步比向其他群体让步更为迫切。1956年，关于在工作岗位劳动动员和惩处怠工的法律被撤销。同年，确立了最低工资，并实行了微薄的退休金。（1964年，退休金甚至扩展到集体农庄农民。）同样在1950年代和1960年代，工作周缩短为五天，产假延长，其他社会保障措施也相继出台。勃列日涅夫治下，这种建立基础福利国家的政策继续实行，而且有所加强，以至于西方一些人把它视为制度“成熟”、从极权秩序演变为仅仅威权秩序的主要标志。
en: In the relaxation after Stalin’s death it was more imperative to make concessions to the workers than to the other groups in the population. In 1956 the laws regarding labor mobilization on the job and criminal penalties for delinquency were withdrawn. The same year, a minimum wage was established and modest retirement pensions were introduced. (In 1964 retirement pensions were even ex tended to the kolkhoz peasantry.) Also in the 1950s and 1960s, the workweek was shortened to five days, maternity leave was extended, and other social security measures were introduced. Under Brezhnev this policy of building a rudimentary welfare state was continued, and indeed somewhat strengthened, to where some in the West took it as a primary sign of the “maturing” of the system, of its evolution from a totalitarian to a merely authoritarian order.

zh: 然而，也许更恰当的看法是，把这些变化视为官名录向工人支付的保护费，以保持制度稳定和安全。因为在赫鲁晓夫治下国家压力的不可避免的放松中，工人变得不安分，具有潜在危险。自1920年代以来第一次出现了野猫罢工，甚至近乎暴动的骚乱。第一起重大事件似乎发生在1959年处女地的新工业城镇铁米尔套。但这场骚动的高潮出现在1962年，那一年赫鲁晓夫“小繁荣”的趋平促使他提高肉类、奶制品和伏特加的价格。这一行动引发了一连串往往暴力的骚乱，从莫斯科地区一直延伸到敖德萨的码头。最严重的骚乱发生在南方城市新切尔卡斯克，那里的罢工被当局严重处理失当，最终以暴力告终，并由克格勃部队镇压（至少七十人被杀）。在派出两名政治局委员恢复秩序后，工人们先因商店里紧急运入的新鲜供应而平静下来，但随后他们的领导人被逮捕并流放到西伯利亚。外部世界直到1975年索尔仁尼琴的《古拉格群岛》出版才知道这一事件。
en: It would perhaps be more appropriate, however, to view these changes as a form of protection money the

paid to the workers to keep the system stable and safe. For in the unavoidable relaxation of state pressure under Khrushchev, the workers had be come restive and potentially dangerous. For the first time since the 1920s, there were wildcat strikes and even riots verging on revolt. The first major incident appears to have occurred in 1959 at Temirtau, a new industrial town in the virgin lands. But the high point of this agitation came in 1962, the year in which the flattening out of Khrushchev’s “mini-boom” led him to raise prices on meat, dairy products, and vodka. This action provoked a string of often violent disturbances extending from the Moscow region to the docks of Odessa. The most serious disturbance occurred in the southern city of Novocherkassk, where a strike, gravely mishandled by the authorities, ended in violence and repression by KGB troops (at least seventy people were killed). After two Politburo members were sent to restore order, the workers were first calmed by the rushing of fresh supplies into the stores, but then their leaders were arrested and shipped off to Siberia. zh: 尽管再没有如此规模的骚乱，但由于工人对工资、住房、食品短缺和劳动定额的不满，重大工人抗议事件一直持续到1980年代。每次当局的反应都一样：他们把事情保密，以免给其他城市树立榜样；临时增加供应来安抚群众；逮捕骚乱领导人。但也需要更实质的让步。虽然计件工资没有完全被计时工资取代，但对工人的生产压力实际上减轻了，最高工资和最低工资工人之间的工资差距也逐渐缩小。这些政策的结果是劳资关系平静——但也是工人生产率的停滞。
en: Although there were no more disturbances of this magnitude, significant industrial incidents continued down into the 1980s because of worker dissatisfaction with pay, housing, food shortages, and labor norms. Each time the authorities’ reaction was the same: They kept the matter secret so it could not set an example for other cities, they bought off the mass with a short spurt of supplies, and they arrested the leaders of the disturbance. But more substantial concessions were also necessary. Although piece-rates were not completely abandoned in favor of time-rates, pressure on workers to produce was in fact lessened, and wage differentials between the highest- and lowest-paid workers were gradually reduced. The result of these policies was labor peace—but also a stagnation of worker productivity.

zh: 斯大林治下苏联工业之所以猛增，一个原因是每名工人的生产率最初非常低；因此，用计件工资的鞭策迅速提高生产率相对容易。然而，在这种最初的生产率上升之后，要实现进一步进步，就需要更微妙的激励。但这一步被计划的僵化和商品的普遍匮乏所阻断。于是，到1970年代初，体制已经接受一支低生产率而就业高度稳定的劳动力，即所谓的“在职失业”。这支冷漠劳动大军的心态，可以用一个很快传遍世界的笑话来概括：一名苏联工人宣称：“他们假装付我工资，我就假装干活。”
en: One reason why Soviet industry had surged under Stalin was an initially very low level of productivity per worker; hence it was relatively easy to raise productivity rapidly with the goad of piece-rates. After this initial rise in productivity, however, subtler incentives would have been required to achieve further progress. But this step was precluded by the rigidity of the Plan and the general scarcity of goods. Thus, by the early 1970s the system had resigned itself to a labor force with low productivity and high security of employment, or what has been called “unemployment on the job.” The mentality of this apathetic labor force came to be summarized in the joke, soon heard around the world, about the Soviet worker who declared: “I’ll pretend to work so long as they pretend to pay me.”

zh: 然而，局势远非笑谈。在勃列日涅夫最后几年，劳动人口实际上处于生物学意义上的衰退状态：男性预期寿命从六十八岁降到六十四岁，婴儿死亡率从3%上升到7%，这在发达国家历史上没有先例。这些不利趋势的一个主要原因是酗酒：酗酒在俄国一直是个问题，此时更变得猖獗，日益影响年轻人口和妇女。烈酒销售占国家收入的15%。这种“收益”的代价，却是更低的工人生产率和社会士气涣散。
en: The situation was far from being a joking matter, however. During Brezhnev’s last years the working population was actually in a state of biological decline: In a case that was without precedent in the history of developed countries, the life expectancy of males fell from sixty-eight to sixty-four years, while the rate of infant mortality increased from 3 to 7 percent. One major cause of these adverse trends was alcoholism: always a problem in Russia, it now became rampant, increasingly affecting younger members of the population as well as women. Sales of spirits accounted for 15 percent of state revenues. The cost of this “gain,” however, was even lower worker productivity and social demoralization.

zh: 勃列日涅夫时期苏联经济中有一个部门，以其自身的方式充满活力并不断增长：“影子”经济或“第二”经济。

这种制度化黑市的历史，当然可以追溯到苏维埃政权的最初年代，当时平行市场及其“背袋贩子”在内战灾难年代对养活国家不可或缺。在斯大林年代长期匮乏中，影子经济一直存在，尽管诉诸它显然也有危险。只是在赫鲁晓夫治下，一个或多或少稳定并半被容忍的第二经济才出现，成为计划的不可或缺的补充：人们不那么害怕了，而国家无法满足它自身政策刺激起来的消费需求。于是，兼职、“干私活”、贪污和“投机”兴盛起来，“寄生虫”也兴盛起来——所谓寄生虫，就是没有正式职业、据称靠这些活动为生的人。这种增长如此迅速，以至于赫鲁晓夫对其中一些行为引入了死刑；死刑偶尔真的被执行，这表明这种商业已经变得多么普遍和肆无忌惮。
en: There was one sector of the Soviet economy during the Brezhnev era that, after its fashion, was dynamic and growing: the “shadow” or “second” economy.

The history of this institutionalized black market, of course, can be traced to the earliest years of Soviet power, when the parallel market and its “bagmen” were indispensable to feeding the country during the disastrous years of the Civil War. During the permanent scarcity of the Stalin years, the shadow economy had been a constant, though it was also obviously a dangerous recourse. It was only under Khrushchev that a more or less stable and semitolerated second economy emerged as the indispensable complement to the Plan: people were now less afraid, and the state could not satisfy the consumer needs that its own policies had sharpened. So moonlighting, work “on the left,” embezzlement, and “speculation” thrived, as did “parasites,” or people without an official occupation who allegedly lived off of these activities. So swift was this growth that Khrushchev introduced the death penalty for some of these practices; that it was actually applied on occasion showed just how widespread and insolent this commerce had become.

zh: 但在勃列日涅夫治下，影子经济成了制度名副其实的支柱。它在两大领域运作，或者可以称为零售贸易和批发贸易。在零售职能中，第二经济通过提供短缺商品，即所谓的“紧俏商品”（defitsitnyi），满足人民的消费需求。它因此提供了国家制度不提供的服务——从裁缝到汽车修理到医疗——并提供人们因质量优越或外国时髦而垂涎的进口商品——从牛仔裤到奢侈品到精密技术。在第二种即批发职能中，影子经济充当官方经济的支持系统，或者充当企业家才智的储备，以弥补计划体制的僵化。当企业无法及时从官方供应商获得完成计划所需的物资时，影子经济便为其提供从原料到备件的各种物品，而这种情况实在太常见。影子企业家经常从一个官方机构挪用或侵吞货物，再卖给另一个机构。有时影子经济甚至升级为家庭用品和工业设备的平行制造。
en: But the shadow economy became a veritable pillar of the system under Brezhnev. It operated in two broad areas, or what might be called retail and wholesale trade. In its retail capacity the second economy catered to the consumer needs of the population by offering goods in short supply, the so-called

items. It thus provided services—from dress making to car repairs to medical attention—that the state system did not provide, and it furnished imported articles—from jeans to luxury items to sophisticated technology—that were coveted for their superior quality or their foreign chic. In its second or wholesale function the shadow economy acted as a support system for the official economy, or as a reserve of entrepreneurial ingenuity to supplement the rigidities of the Plan. Thus, it provided state enter prises with everything from raw materials to spare parts on those all-too-numerous occasions when an enterprise could not get necessary items from official suppliers fast enough to meet its plan. Shadow entrepreneurs would frequently siphon off or embezzle goods from one agency of the official system to sell to another. And at times the shadow economy even graduated into parallel manufacturing of household goods and industrial equipment.

zh: 第二经济就这样常常产生名副其实的“黑手党”，这个词在勃列日涅夫时期被吸收进当代俄语。这些黑手党有时甚至与党的等级体系重叠，形成一种共生关系：企业家获得政治保护，以换取物质商品和服务。因为在一个经济制度首先是政治制度的世界里，政治权力成了财富的首要来源。的确，在一些边疆共和国，黑手党实际上接管了地方党，或者更准确地说，地方党在很大程度上把自己变成了黑手党。最著名的例子也许是格鲁吉亚，当时的第一书记、政治局候补委员瓦西里·姆扎瓦纳泽最终被该共和国内务部长爱德华·谢瓦尔德纳泽赶下台。但一个更引人注目的例子是乌兹别克斯坦的党委书记拉菲克·阿杜洛夫，他养着一群妻妾，还设有一间对付批评者的刑讯室；而乌兹别克共和国的党委头目则虚报棉花产量，莫斯科据此付钱给他。但腐败也出现在制度的最上层，勃列日涅夫的亲信和亲属组成的“第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克黑手党”便是例子。这一事实部分地为民众所知，从而进一步削弱了政权的可信度。
en: In this way the second economy often generated veritable “mafias,” a word adopted into current Russian under Brezhnev. These mafias sometimes even overlapped with the Party hierarchy to create a symbiosis wherein entrepreneurs received political protection in exchange for material goods and services. For in a world where the economic system was in the first instance a political one, political power became a prime source of wealth. Indeed, in some of the border republics the mafia virtually took over the local Party, or more accurately, the local Party largely turned itself into a mafia. Perhaps the most famous case was that of Georgia under First Secretary and alternate Politburo member Vasilii Mzhavanadze, who was finally driven from power by the republic’s interior minister, Edvard She vardnadze. But an even more picturesque example was provided by Rafik Adulov, a Party secretary in Uzbekistan, who kept a harem and had a torture chamber for his critics, while the Uzbek republic Party boss inflated the cotton production figures for which Moscow paid him. But corruption could also be found at the very top of the system—in the “Dnepropetrovsk mafia” of Brezhnev’s own cronies and kin—a fact that was partially known to the population and thus diminished the regime’s credibility even further.

zh: 这些弊端并非出于偶然，正如苏联农业的失败并非由于坏天气。机关的黑手党化在勃列日涅夫治下成为重大问题，因为他的“干部稳定”政策，而这一政策又源于党作为一个制度的长期演变；同样的原因产生了新的老年政治现象，它在苏联权力体系顶端格外显眼，在各级机构也很普遍。
en: Nor were these failings due to accident any more than were the failings of Soviet agriculture due to bad weather. “Mafiazation” of the apparat became a major problem under Brezhnev because of his policy of “stability of cadres,” which in turn derived from the long-term evolution of the Party as an institution; and these same causes produced the new phenomenon of gerontocracy, which was so visible at the top of the Soviet hierarchy yet also prevalent at every level.

zh: 犯罪行为也有其经济逻辑，这种逻辑源于指令性计划的本质。苏联实验在勃列日涅夫治下已过半个世纪，到那时已经证明，不可能压制市场：尽管一切努力，市场总是回来，无论是列宁战时共产主义下非法的“背袋贩子”，还是他的新经济政策下合法的市场，或者斯大林治下的家庭自留地和集体农庄市场。但实验也证明，确实有可能把市场无限期地驱入地下，从而使它在法律上和实际社会行为上都成为犯罪。但由于这个地下市场是由真实的社会需求创造并回应这些需求的，而不是粗俗的“投机”，它在某种程度上涉及全体人口；因此每个人都在某种程度上受到刑事追究的威胁，因为每个人都必须有一点“门路”或“交易”才能生存。西方当然也有腐败，但在那里腐败是选择性的；一个人不必靠它生存。在前苏联，仅仅为了过日子，腐败成了生活所必需的。因此每个人总是有某种罪过，而不可或缺的活动遭到污名化和限制。
en: Criminal behavior had an economic logic as well, one that derived from the very nature of directive planning. The Soviet experiment, which under Brezhnev passed the half-century mark, had by then demonstrated that it was impossible to suppress the market: despite all efforts it kept coming back, whether illegally with the “bagmen” under Lenin’s War Communism or legally during his NEP, or under Stalin with the family plot and the kolkhoz market. Yet the experiment had also demonstrated that it

possible to drive the market underground indefinitely and thereby make it criminal, both as a matter of law and as a matter of actual social behavior. But since this underground market was created by, and responded to, genuine social needs, not crass “speculation,” it to some degree involved the whole population; thus everyone was criminalized in some measure, for everyone had to have a little “racket” or “deal” in order to survive. There is also corruption in the West, of course, but there it is optional; one does not have to engage in it to survive. In the former Soviet Union it was mandatory just in order to get by. So everyone was always guilty of something, and an indispensable activity was stigmatized and stunted.

zh: 第二经济有多大？从来没有哪位有声望的经济学家试图给出一个数字，尽管它存在的证据无处不在；但这种不可避免的不确定性，只是我们对整个苏联经济不确定性的一个更严重的例子。从数量上说，关于平行经济最多只能说它相当可观；但重要的是，从性质上说，它对整个制度的运转不可或缺。它不是政权所坚称的那种可以由更好的政策或更严格的纪律纠正的缺陷或弊端的产物。它是人为的国家经济垄断的不可避免的后果，同时也是使这种垄断本身得以维持的不可或缺的手段。把这些不可或缺的职能交给警察处理，结果不仅阻碍了官方和地下经济，而且破坏了公众道德和民众的法律意识。这是计划的“合理性”的又一代价。
en: How large was the second economy? No reputable economist has ever attempted to put a figure on it, although evidence of its existence was everywhere; but this unavoidable uncertainty is only an aggravated case of our uncertainty about the Soviet economy as a whole. Quantitatively, the most one can say of the parallel economy is that it was quite considerable; but the important thing is that, qualitatively, it was indispensable to the functioning of the overall system. It was not a deficiency or a product of abuses that could be corrected by better policies or more stringent discipline, as the regime maintained. It was the unavoidable consequence of an artificial state economic monopoly, as well as the indispensable means for permitting that monopoly itself to carry on. The result of making these indispensable functions a matter for the police was not only to hobble the economy, both official and underground, but to undermine public morality and the sense of law among the population. And this was another cost of the Plan’s “rationality.”

zh: 全球强权的负担
en: THE BURDEN OF GLOBAL POWER

zh: 制度经济的缺陷，恰恰在它唯一具有国际竞争力的部门——军工生产——中得到凸显。正如我们已经看到的，苏联经济所有部门的组织方式都是军事式的，但为军事目的的实际生产只是在1937年以后才成为其主要职能。诚然，考虑到从那时到1945年的国际环境，这完全可以理解。然而在战后，情况大不相同，军事力量在制度中的核心地位变得更加持久和制度化。因为苏联此时不是受到邻近对手的直接威胁，而是为了在欧洲和东亚相对于“帝国主义阵营”的“实力地位”进行长期谋划。冲突方式也变了，因为冷战不是一场真正要打的较量，而是一场必须不断为之做准备的较量。由此产生的和平时期长达四十年的永久军事技术动员，在国际冲突史上大概是独一无二的现象。这场冲突的负担当然也落在美国“一方”，但在苏联，冷战所消耗的国家资源比例要大得多。在勃列日涅夫年代尤其如此。
en: The defects of the system’s economy are only highlighted by the one sector where it was internationally competitive, military production. As we have seen, the mode of organization of the Soviet economy in all sectors was military, but actual production for military purposes became its chief function only after 1937. To be sure, given international circumstances from then until 1945, this was only understandable. In the postwar period, however, circumstances were quite different, and the centrality of military power to the system acquired a more enduring, institutionalized character. For the Soviet Union was now not directly menaced by a nearby adversary but engaged in long-term maneuvering for “positions of strength” in Europe and East Asia vis-à-vis the “camp of imperialism.” And the mode of conflict had also changed, since the Cold War was not a contest actually to be fought but one constantly to be prepared for. The resulting four decades of permanent military-technological mobilization during peacetime is probably a unique phenomenon in the history of international conflict. The burden of this conflict, of course, also fell on the American “side,” but in the Soviet Union the Cold War effort consumed a far larger proportion of national resources. And this was especially true during the Brezhnev years.

zh: 1945年后，苏联的复员程度几乎与美国相当。苏联的重新动员只是由于朝鲜战争才开始，然后在1950年代末，如前所述，赫鲁晓夫再次削减军力，同时试图在导弹力量上迅速赶上美国。只是在1960年代，在危险的古巴事件之后，苏联才开始长期、系统地扩充军备，以全面匹配或超过美国的军事力量。这首先意味着常备地面部队永久增加到四百万人以上。在海军元帅谢尔盖·戈尔什科夫指导下，这也意味着建立一支世界级海军——尤其是潜艇舰队——能够在全球各大洋活动。最后，这意味着在核武器和弹道导弹上与美国平起平坐。到1969年，苏联终于达到了渴望已久的地位：它第一次真正成为一个平起平坐的超级大国。
en: After 1945 the Soviet Union demobilized almost as much as the United States. Soviet remobilization began only as a result of the Korean War, and then in the late 1950s, as already indicated, Khrushchev cut the military again while he attempted to catch up quickly with the United States in missile strength. It was only in the 1960s, after the dangerous Cuban episode, that the Soviet Union settled down for the long haul of a systematic arms buildup to match or surpass American military strength across the board. This meant, first, a permanent increase of ground forces to something over four million men. Under the direction of Admiral Sergei Gorshkov, it also meant the creation of a world-class navy—and especially a submarine fleet—capable of operating in all the oceans of the planet. It meant, finally, nuclear and ballistic parity with the United States. And by 1969 the Soviet Union had at last reached that long-coveted status: For the first time, it was truly a coequal superpower.

zh: 由于政权的野心是不惜一切代价维持这一地位，如有可能还要把它变成优势，军备竞赛在勃列日涅夫和安德罗波夫年代达到了顶点。这一时期的苏联被描述为一个不是拥有军工复合体、而是本身就是军工复合体的国家。但更准确的说法是，它是一个党—军—工复合体，因为军方并不掌权，军备建设的原因并非来自战略考虑本身，而是来自党对世界分裂为两个敌对阵营的政治认识。只有党进行全面社会动员的能力，才能产生勃列日涅夫治下所达到的那种庞大军工复合体。
en: Because the regime’s ambition was to maintain this rank at all costs, and if possible to turn it into superiority, the arms race proceeded to its culmination during the Brezhnev and Andropov years. The Soviet Union during this period has been described as a state that did not
a military-industrial complex but

a military-industrial complex. But it would be more accurate to say that it was a Party-military-industrial complex, for the military was not in charge, and the reasons for the arms buildup did not derive from strategic considerations per se but from the Party’s political perception of a world divided into two hostile camps. And only the Party’s capacity for total social mobilization could produce a military-industrial complex of the huge dimensions achieved under Brezhnev.

zh: 在此期间，中央情报局估计苏联军费约占苏联国民生产总值的15%，而美国的军费平均占5%。但1990年，外交部长谢瓦尔德纳泽声称苏联的真实数字是25%，公开性时代其他苏联估计甚至高达40%。
尽管谢瓦尔德纳泽肯定比中央情报局更接近事实，我们仍然不知道苏联国民生产总值有多大比例用于军事，因为苏联人自己从未真正知道。的确，有理由相信他们用中央情报局的数字来计算自己的国民生产总值，因此错误地认为自己拥有比实际更大的军费余地。与此同时，劳动力中极大比例的人在某种程度上参与了军事工作：至少25%，阿甘别吉扬和其他苏联经济学家声称高达30%或40%，而在美国和其他西方国家，相应数字低于5%。
无论如何，苏联“国防”这种不产生经济效益的活动所占用人力和物力资源的比例绝对是压倒性的，它排除了整个国家任何形式的经济复兴。
en: During this period the CIA estimated that the Soviet military absorbed some 15 percent of the USSR’s GNP, whereas in the United States military expenditure averaged 5 percent. But in 1990 Foreign Minister Shevardnadze claimed that the true Soviet figure had been 25 percent, and other Soviet estimates of the
era went as high as 40 percent.

Although Shevardnadze was surely closer to the mark than the CIA had been, we still do not know how large a percentage of Soviet GNP went to the military because the Soviets themselves never really knew. Indeed, there is reason to believe that they used the CIA’s figures to calculate their own GNP, and therefore erroneously believed they had a wider margin for military expenditure than they actually possessed. At the same time, an inordinate proportion of the labor force was involved to some extent in work for the military: it was at least 25 percent, and Aganbegyan and other Soviet economists claim it was as high as 30 or 40 percent, whereas in the United States and other Western countries the corresponding figure was below 5 percent.

In any event, the proportion of human and material resources taken up by the sterile activity of Soviet “defense” was absolutely crushing, and it precluded any kind of economic revival for the country at large.

zh: 此外，军方拥有最先进的技术、最高质量的装备和国内许多最出色的人才，因为这些都是通过政治命令分配给它的。军方还可以说是“需求方”实体：与平民不同，它是一个可以拒绝劣质产品的消费者，从而迫使计划作出有利于自己的修改。它需要这项权利，因为它的产品——同样与民用部门不同——必须在国际上具有竞争力，无论是在中东战场上还是在第三世界的军火市场上。四分之一世纪里，苏联军队以惊人的技术和组织能力，确实是世界历史上最庞大、最强大的两支武装力量之一。从某种意义上说，这是党国的最高成就，也是这种制度唯一能够出色完成的任务。但这也是一项超出制度实际经济能力的成就，因此无法长期维持。而比任何其他单一因素都更重要的是，政权维持其超级大国地位的企图，将触发1989—1991年的崩溃。
en: Furthermore, the military had at its disposal the most-advanced technology, the highest-quality equipment, and many of the sharpest minds in the country because these were allocated to it by political fiat. The military was also what might be called a “demand side” entity: unlike the civilian population, it was a consumer that could refuse products it found inferior, and thus force a revision of the Plan in its favor. It required this right because its products—again unlike those of the civilian sector—had to be competitive internationally, whether on the battlefields of the Middle East or in the arms markets of the Third World. And for a quarter century, in a prodigious display of technological and organizational prowess, the Soviet military was indeed one of the two largest and most powerful ensembles of armed forces in the history of the world. In a sense, this was the supreme achievement of the Party-state, the only kind of task such a system could excel at. But it was also an achievement that was beyond the system’s real economic capacity, and thus it could not be sustained for long. And more than any other single factor, it was the regime’s attempt to sustain its superpower status that would trigger the collapse of 1989-1991.

zh: 几乎与这种军事努力同样具有毁灭性的，是它所服务的外交政策。赫鲁晓夫在古巴的冒险之后，勃列日涅夫—柯西金政府采取了更谨慎的外交政策。但政权的主要目标与赫鲁晓夫相同：与美国达成妥协，使苏联得以在国内积聚力量。然而，朝这一目标的努力不断被政权的次要目标打乱，即利用第三世界的革命和民族解放运动，从而以美国为代价增强苏联的力量和威望。毕竟，这是莫斯科的天职，无论作为世界革命领袖还是作为超级大国。放弃国外的有利机会，会自动削弱苏联在全世界的实力，并减少国内社会和意识形态动员的必要性。反对“帝国主义”的不懈斗争，一如以往，对维持党国的内部平衡不可或缺。
en: Almost as ruinous as this military effort was the foreign policy it served. After Khrushchev’s adventure in Cuba, the Brezhnev-Kosygin government adopted a more cautious foreign policy. But the regime’s primary aim was the same as Khrushchev’s: to achieve an accommodation with the United States that would allow the Soviet Union to build up its strength at home. Yet efforts toward this end were constantly disrupted by the regime’s secondary aim, which was to profit from Third World revolutionary and national liberation movements and thereby enhance Soviet power and prestige at the expense of the United States. This, after all, was Moscow’s vocation, both as a world revolutionary leader and as a superpower. Foregoing favorable opportunities abroad would have automatically diminished Soviet power throughout the world and reduced the need for social and ideological mobilization at home. The unending struggle against “imperialism” was, as ever, indispensable for maintaining the internal equilibrium of the Party-state.

zh: 苏联在勃列日涅夫年代的大多数海外冒险都是代理人冒险。第一个主要活动地区是中东。苏联自1948年起就卷入那里，当时它是第一个承认以色列的大国，这一行动本质上是为了削弱英国的“帝国主义”。但此后几乎立即，斯大林就转而支持“反犹太复国主义”，部分是因为他把苏联犹太人对以色列的惊人热情视为对苏联的不忠，部分是因为这是煽动对以色列的新靠山美国的敌意的一种手段。后来，赫鲁晓夫把这一政策扩展到积极支持阿拉伯人；他使苏联成为埃及和叙利亚、后来又成为伊拉克和利比亚的靠山和军事供应者，勃列日涅夫继续了这一政策。然而，其目的不是让阿拉伯人战胜以色列，而是动员该地区反对英国和法国，然后反对美国。莫斯科首先把这一代价高昂的政策集中于埃及。当安瓦尔·萨达特1972年把苏联顾问全部逐出埃及，并在不久后转向美国寻求资金和军事供应时，苏联的重点便转向了“革命的”阿拉伯独裁政权。
en: Most of the Soviet Union’s foreign adventures in the Brezhnev years were proxy adventures. The first major area of activity was the Middle East. The Soviet Union had been involved there since 1948, when she was the first major power to recognize Israel, an action undertaken essentially to undermine British “imperialism.” But almost immediately thereafter, Stalin took up the cause of “anti-Zionism,” in part because he viewed the Soviet Jewish population’s surprising enthusiasm for Israel as tantamount to disloyalty to the USSR, and in part because it was a means of stimulating hostility towards Israel’s new patron, the United States. Later, Khrushchev extended this policy to include active support of the Arabs; he made the Soviet Union the patron and military supplier of Egypt and Syria, and later of Iraq and Libya, a policy that Brezhnev continued. Its aim, however, was not to produce an Arab victory over Israel, but to mobilize the area against Britain and France and then the United States. Moscow first focused this costly policy on Egypt. When Anwar Sadat expelled all Soviet advisors from Egypt in 1972 and soon thereafter turned to the Americans for funding and military supplies, the Soviet focus then shifted to the “revolutionary” Arab dictatorships.

zh: 苏联活动的第二个主要地区是东南亚。1954年，第一次印度支那战争，也就是法国参与的越南战争，以越南分为南北两部分而告终。根据当年的日内瓦协议，本应举行全国选举以统一越南，但直到1960年代初，西方普遍认为该国实际上会像朝鲜或德国一样保持分裂。然而，北越完全打算接管南方，无论有无选举。在统一选举未能举行后，河内——在中国积极鼓励下——开始组织南越“解放阵线”。美国随即采取行动保卫南越。由于中国太弱，无法对抗这样的对手，1965年河内转向另一个超级大国寻求装备。莫斯科欣然应允，既为了压过中国，也为了削弱其美国对手。
en: The second major area of Soviet activity was Southeast Asia. In 1954 the first, or French, Vietnam War ended with the country being partitioned into a North and a South. According to the Geneva agreements of that year, national elections were to be held to unify Vietnam, but until the early 1960s it was generally assumed in the West that the country would in fact remain divided, like Korea or Germany. North Vietnam, however, fully intended to take over the South, with or without elections. After it proved impossible to organize elections, Hanoi—with the active encouragement of China—began to organize a South Vietnamese “liberation front.” The United States then moved to defend South Vietnam. Because China was too weak to counter such an adversary, in 1965 Hanoi turned to the other superpower for equipment. Moscow willingly complied, both to outflank the Chinese and to undermine its American rival.

zh: 结果是勃列日涅夫年代最有利可图的外交冒险。美国因害怕像在朝鲜那样把中国卷入，并希望避免与苏联直接冲突，进行了一场规模相对受限的战争。这一战略有双重不利：它极具破坏性，却又可悲地不足以威慑北方或粉碎越共。因此冲突拖到1960年代末；它分裂了美国舆论，侵蚀了反共决心，并且按照苏联的看法，使“力量对比”朝着有利于他们的方向转变。与此同时，华盛顿需要莫斯科帮助，让河内接受谈判，以保全面子的方式结束冲突，这种需要增强了苏联的国际地位。
en: The result was the most profitable foreign policy adventure of the Brezhnev years. The United States, fearful of drawing in the Chinese, as in Korea, and wishing to avoid a direct clash with the Soviets, fought a relatively limited war. This strategy had the double disadvantage of being terribly destructive and yet woefully inadequate either to deter the North or to crush the Vietcong. The conflict therefore dragged on until the end of the decade; it divided opinion and eroded anti-Communist resolve in the United States, and, as the Soviets perceived it, shifted the “correlation of forces” in their favor. At the same time, Washington needed Moscow’s help in getting Hanoi to accept negotiations for a face-saving end to the conflict, and this need strengthened the Soviet Union’s international position.

zh: 莫斯科最终确实帮助促成了谈判，使美国得以在1973年撤出该地区，北方军队却仍留在南方；因此冲突随时可以按照更有利于北方的条件重新开始。而这正是1975年发生的事。虽然苏联没有策划北方征服南方，但他们没有采取任何行动约束盟友，而整个行动之所以可能，完全有赖于苏联向北越提供了重型装备。因此，按照勃列日涅夫所说的“两种制度之间的阶级斗争”来衡量，越南战争是苏联的一场伟大胜利，尽管是代理人的胜利。
en: Moscow eventually did help produce the negotiations that permitted the United States to withdraw from the area in 1973 yet left a Northern military presence in the South; hence the conflict could resume at any time on terms more favorable to the North. And this is just what occurred in 1975. Although the Soviets did not instigate the North’s conquest of the South, they did nothing to restrain their ally, and the whole operation was possible only because the Soviets had supplied the North with heavy equipment. Thus, in terms of what Brezhnev called the “class struggle between the two systems,” the Vietnam War was a great, if vicarious, Soviet victory.

zh: 同一时期，苏联的另一个巨大对手中国，被有效地排除了大国竞争。产生这一结果的过程始于印度尼西亚的事件。1960年代初，印尼共产党是仅次于苏联和中国的世界第三大共产党。苏加诺总统让该国退出联合国，作为与中国一起建立新的第三世界国际组织的前奏，而中国进入联合国则被美国阻止。苏加诺和印尼共产党随后尝试内部政变，以建立“进步的”独裁。此举适得其反，印尼军方彻底消灭了共产主义运动，在此过程中至少杀死十万人。莫斯科甚至没有向苏哈托将军的新印尼政权提出抗议；毕竟，这场屠杀只是中国的失败。
en: During the same years, the Soviet Union’s other great adversary, China, was effectively eliminated from great-power competition. The process that produced this outcome began with events in Indonesia, which at the beginning of the 1960s had the largest Communist Party in the world after those of the Soviet Union and China. President Sukarno withdrew his country from the United Nations as a preliminary to setting up a new Third World international organization with China, whose entry into the UN was barred by the United States. Sukarno and the Indonesian Communists then attempted an internal coup to establish a “progressive” dictatorship. This backfired, and the Indonesian military completely liquidated the Communist movement, killing at least one hundred thousand people in the process. Moscow did not even lodge a protest with the new Indonesian regime of General Suharto; the massacre, after all, was only a defeat for China.

zh: 中国的下一次失败是自作自受，其形式是1966—1969年文化大革命的大动荡。这一事件在自我毁灭的狂怒上只有斯大林的清洗可与之相比，它在很大程度上使中国作为对立的革命模式失去了信誉，并削弱了它作为经济和有抱负的全球大国的地位。然后，1972年，随着尼克松访华，毛泽东做了他先前曾为此诅咒赫鲁晓夫的事：他与美国改善关系。最后，1976年毛泽东去世，导致四人帮统治下的新动荡，从而进一步在国际上失去信誉。虽然邓小平在十年末的“修正主义”结束了这场动乱，但它也终结了中国在第三世界眼中的革命神话。于是，莫斯科终于恢复了“国际无产阶级运动”的领导权。
en: China’s next defeat was self-inflicted and took the form of the great convulsion of the Cultural Revolution of 1966-1969. This episode, comparable in its self-destructive fury only to Stalin’s purges, largely discredited China as a rival revolutionary model and weakened her as an economy and an aspiring global power. Then, in 1972, with Nixon’s visit to China, Mao did what he had earlier anathematized Khrushchev for doing: he entered into a rapprochement with the United States. Finally, Mao’s death in 1976 led to new turbulence under the Gang of Four, and thus to further international discredit. Although Deng Xiaoping’s “revisionism” at the end of the decade brought this turmoil to a close, it also ended the Chinese revolutionary myth in the eyes of the Third World. Thus Moscow at last recovered the leadership of the “international proletarian movement.”
