zh: 结果，新统一的越南最终成为莫斯科的盟友和中国的积极敌人。这一转变大大提高了苏联在第三世界和本国人民眼中的威望，即使其实际力量未必因此增强。但这场胜利也有负面：国际共产主义运动已被如此多的分裂和叛离撕碎，不再作为一支革命力量具有多大可信度。事实上，到1970年，第二次世界大战点燃的一系列真正的革命烽火已基本熄灭，而“国际”共产主义本质上只剩下苏联在全球投射军事力量的能力。尽管如此，这已足以使1970年代成为苏联全球影响力和实力的最高点。世界主导权、甚至彻底胜利，从未显得如此接近实现。正是这种对“两个阵营”之间“力量对比”的认知，构成了1970年代缓和的背景。
en: In consequence, newly united Vietnam wound up as Moscow’s ally and an active foe of China. This turn of events greatly increased the Soviet Union’s prestige, if not its actual power, in the Third World and in the eyes of its own population. But there was also a negative side to this victory: the international Communist movement, having been rent by so many schisms and defections, was no longer very credible as a revolutionary force. In fact, by 1970 the series of authentic revolutionary flare-ups ignited by the Second World War had largely ended, and “international” Communism consisted essentially of the Soviet Union’s ability to project military power around the world. Still, this was quite enough to make the 1970s the high point of Soviet global influence and strength. Never had world predominance, or even outright victory, seemed nearer to attainment. It is this perception of the “correlation of forces” between the “two camps” that was the context for détente in the 1970s.

zh: 随着1969年后越南战争逐渐结束，认真恢复与美国的谈判、回到古巴危机和1963年《禁止核试验条约》之后出现的缓和，成为可能。谈判促成了核武器发明以来第一个重大军备控制协议——1972年的《第一阶段限制战略武器条约》（SALT I），它限制了反弹道导弹（ABM）的部署，并对洲际弹道导弹规定了非常高的上限。可以说，这项协议只是把双方本来就打算做的事情正式化，但它至少把竞争限制在外交范围内。本着同样的精神，1972年尼克松总统访问莫斯科期间，双方就“和平共处”的“基本原则”达成一致，其中每一方都承诺不“以损害对方为代价单方面谋取利益”。最后，缓和意味着经济纽带：华盛顿将给予莫斯科最惠国贸易地位，并鼓励外国对苏联投资。
en: With the winding down of the Vietnam War after 1969, it became possible to seriously resume negotiations with the Americans and return to the detente that had followed in the wake of the Cuban crisis and the Test Ban Treaty of 1963. Negotiations led to the first major arms control agreement since the invention of nuclear weapons—the SALT I Treaty of 1972—which limited antiballistic missile (ABM) deployments and established very high ceilings on ICBMs. Arguably, this agreement only formalized what the two sides were intending to do anyway, but it at least kept the rivalry within the bounds of diplomacy. In the same spirit, during President Nixon’s visit to Moscow in 1972, the two sides agreed on “Basic Principles” of “peaceful coexistence” in which each country pledged to refrain from taking “unilateral advantage at the expense of the other.” Finally, détente meant economic bonds: Washington was to accord Moscow most-favored-nation trade status, and foreign investment in the Soviet Union was to be encouraged.

zh: 在西方方面，这些政策背后的想法是，通过促进东西方利益的一致来安抚苏联人并使其行为温和化。按照这种推理，如果苏联通过互利军备控制协议被系入国际体系，通过贸易被系入世界经济，那么它就会出于自身利益而在其他问题上同美国和西欧合作。正如亨利·基辛格所说：“随着时间推移，贸易和投资或许会潜移默化地改变苏联制度自给自足的倾向，并通过苏联经济与世界经济的逐步结合，培育出一定程度的相互依赖，为政治格局增添稳定的因素。”
当代西德总理维利·勃兰特的“东方政策”也基于类似理由：通过减少紧张和建立信任，该政策旨在使东欧各政权、特别是东德政权变得温和并实行改革。
en: On the Western side, the idea behind these policies was to reassure the Soviets and moderate their behavior by fostering a congruence of interests between East and West. If the Soviet Union, so the reasoning went, was tied into the international system by mutually advantageous arms control agreements and into the world economy by trade, she would then have a stake of self-interest in cooperating with the United States and Western Europe on other issues. As Henry Kissinger put the matter: “Over time, trade and investment may leaven the autarchic tendencies of the Soviet system, and by gradual association of the Soviet economy with the world economy, foster a degree of interdependence that adds an element of stability to the political equation.”
A similar rationale underlay the contemporary
of West German Chancellor Willy Brandt: by reducing tension and building trust, the policy was intended to mellow and reform the East European regimes, and in particular that of East Germany.

zh: 因此，整个1970年代，西方企业大量投资于东方，尤其是哥穆尔卡较温和的继任者爱德华·盖莱克治下的波兰。但结果并没有产生走向与西方经济利益趋同的进展；它只是通过以资金制造暂时的虚假繁荣，使一个已经失去信誉的波兰政权又支撑了十年。同样，社民党对瓦尔特·乌布利希和埃里希·昂纳克的支持确实以金钱换取了东德异见者移居西方，但并没有软化东德的内部结构；相反，这一政策助长了一种幻觉，即东德是一个真正成功的共产主义经济和世界第十工业强国。因此，在这两个案例中都没有形成利益一致；相反，两国出现的都是对西方的经济依赖，而没有相应的政治立场的相应调整。但这对于经济政策源于政治关切、而不是像基辛格和勃兰特所设想的那样政治源于经济的制度来说，是意料之中的。
en: Consequently, throughout the 1970s Western business invested extensively in the East, and especially in Poland under Gomulka’s more moderate successor, Edward Gierek. But the result was not to produce progress towards a convergence of economic interests with the West; it was to bolster for another decade an already discredited Polish regime by financing a temporary false prosperity. Similarly, SPD support for Walter Ulbricht and Erich Honecker did permit East German dissidents to emigrate to the West in exchange for money, but it did not soften East Germany’s internal structures; indeed, this policy contributed to the illusion that East Germany was a genuinely successful Communist economy and the tenth-largest industrial power in the world. So no congruence of interests developed in either of these cases; rather, what emerged in both countries was a form of economic dependence on the West without a corresponding political realignment. But this was only to be expected of systems where economic policy derives from political concerns, and not the other way around as both Kissinger and Brandt assumed.

zh: 因此，在苏联方面，缓和与东方政策的这场赌博的意义与西方截然不同。诚然，它是避免核冲突危险的一种手段。但它也是一种缓解东方相对经济衰退和日益扩大的技术落后、而不招致任何政治依赖的手段。
en: On the Soviet side, therefore, the wager of détente and

had a very different meaning from that in the West. It was, to be sure, a means for obviating the danger of nuclear conflict. But it was also a means for palliating the East’s relative economic decline and growing technological lag without incurring any political dependency.

zh: 在这方面，最伟大的先驱项目是1966年在伏尔加河畔陶里亚蒂由意大利出资兴建的菲亚特汽车厂。1970年代，美国出资在卡马河畔兴建的卡车厂，以及用斯托利奇纳亚伏特加支付的百事可乐工厂，只是持续外国投资中最著名的例子；但苏联还大量获得了计算机和先进电子技术。所有这些都由1973年欧佩克石油禁运后流向莫斯科的“石油美元”横财提供资金，因为苏联是世界上最大的石油生产国。石油美元还支付了弥补苏联农业不足所必需的粮食进口。因此，在苏联经济衰落之际，政权却能够通过与西方建立一种寄生性经济关系，在政治上保持与西方的竞争力。
en: In this regard, the great pioneer project was the Italian-financed Fiat automobile works constructed at Togliatti, on the Volga, in 1966. In the 1970s the American-financed truck factory on the Kama, and the Pepsi Cola factories paid for with Stolichnaia vodka, were only the best-known examples of continuing foreign investment; but the Soviet Union also made significant acquisitions of computer and advanced electronic technology. All of this was financed by the bonanza of “petrodollars” that came Moscow’s way after OPEC’s oil embargo of 1973, for the Soviet Union was the largest producer of petroleum in the world. And petrodollars also paid for the grain imports that were necessary to make up for the deficiencies of Soviet agriculture. Thus, at a time when the Soviet economy was declining, the regime was nonetheless able to remain politically competitive with the West by entering into a parasitical economic relationship with it.

zh: 此外，这一切都发生在西方命运处于二战以来最低谷的时候。1973年的石油冲击结束了战后四分之一世纪的繁荣，即世界历史上最大的经济扩张。美国在越南的失败和水门丑闻同时动摇了西方的政治地位。对莫斯科来说，它从未停止相信资本主义的内部矛盾总有一天会摧毁它，这些事件看起来并非不合情理地像是根本危机的开端。于是，缓和成了莫斯科促成这场危机的手段，其方式是诱使西方在“两种制度之间的意识形态斗争”中放松警惕。就此而言，缓和类似于苏联人周期性地诉诸的和平攻势，作为削弱对手的意识形态手段。因为勃列日涅夫的“紧张局势缓和”（西方译为“缓和”），就像赫鲁晓夫的“和平共处”一样，并不意味着国际关系不再是“阶级斗争”的一种形式——这场斗争只有到社会主义胜利才会结束。这些意识形态主题也不是西方一些人所设想的那种在核时代不必当真的革命修辞残余。只要勃列日涅夫、柯西金和苏斯洛夫这一斯大林培养的一代仍在掌权，对“国际阶级斗争”的信仰就是政策的真实指南。而其具体目标是把美国逐出欧亚大陆。
en: Furthermore, all of this occurred when the West’s fortunes were at their lowest ebb since the Second World War. The petroleum shock of 1973 ended the quarter-century prosperity of the postwar period, the greatest economic expansion in world history. The American defeat in Vietnam and the Watergate scandal simultaneously shook the West’s political position. To Moscow, which had never ceased believing that the internal contradictions of capitalism would one day destroy it, these events appeared, not implausibly, as the beginnings of fundamental crisis. So détente became a means for Moscow to contribute to this crisis by inducing the West to relax its vigilance in the “ideological struggle between the two systems.” As such, détente was akin to the peace offensives to which the Soviets periodically resorted as an ideological means of undermining the adversary. For Brezhnev’s “relaxation of tensions” (which the West translated as détente), like Khrushchev’s “peaceful coexistence,” did not mean that international relations had become any less a form of the “class struggle” that would end only with the victory of socialism. Nor were these ideological themes mere vestiges of revolutionary rhetoric that was not to be taken seriously in a nuclear age, as some in the West supposed. So long as the Stalin-bred generation of Brezhnev, Kosygin, and Suslov remained in charge, the belief in the “international class struggle” was a real guide to policy. And its concrete aim was to expell the United States from Eurasia.

zh: 总之，对西方来说，缓和是逐步超越冷战的方式；对东方来说，则是逐步赢得冷战的方式。双方都下了赌注，但结果事态既没有按照西方的期望发展，也没有按照东方的期望发展。1970年代前半期，西方的剧本似乎正在实现；1970年代后半期，东方的剧本似乎接近实现。但到1980年代初，冷战全面卷土重来。
en: In sum, for the West détente was a gradual way to transcend the Cold War; for the East it was a gradual way to win it. Both sides had made a bet, but, as it turned out, events followed the expectations of neither. In the first half of the 1970s, the West’s scenario seemed to be coming about; in the second half of the decade, the East’s scenario seemed close to realization. But in the early 1980s, the Cold War returned in full force.

zh: 1950年代和1960年代初，在赫鲁晓夫治下，苏联人强硬到好斗的程度，因为社会主义阵营不能接受美国从“实力地位”进行谈判的妄称。1960年代和1970年代初，在勃列日涅夫治下，他们把自己的实力建设到与美国相当的水平，因此能够接受带来第一阶段限制战略武器协议与缓和的谈判。然而，随着1970年代推移，“力量对比”似乎朝着有利于苏联的方向转变，于是到那个十年临近结束时，他们自己也采取“从实力地位出发”的行动。这一转变始于1975年南越的陷落和赫尔辛基协议的签署。
en: In the 1950s and early 1960s, under Khrushchev, the Soviets had been tough to the point of truculence because the camp of socialism could not submit to the American pretension of negotiating “from positions of strength.” In the 1960s and early 1970s, under Brezhnev, they had built up their strength to the level of that of the United States and could therefore accept the negotiations leading to SALT I and détente. As the 1970s progressed, however, the “correlation of forces” seemed to shift in favor of the Soviets, so toward the end of that decade they themselves took to acting “from positions of strength.” The shift began with the fall of South Vietnam and the signing of the Helsinki agreements in 1975.

zh: 赫尔辛基欧洲安全与合作会议是缓和的高潮，也是苏联实现其长期抱负的时刻：使欧洲现有边界获得正式承认——也就是说，在没有德国和平条约的情况下，让西方接受苏联的战后收益及其“阵营”不可侵犯。诚然，他们不得不接受“第三篮子”，承诺尊重人权。他们把这视为纯粹的形式，但东欧集团的异见者很快就会利用这一承诺，通过组织“赫尔辛基观察小组”来推进他们的事业。但与其外部帝国获得国际合法化这一巨大收获相比，这只是一个小小的烦恼。
en: The Helsinki Conference on Security and Cooperation in Europe was the high point of détente and the occasion on which the Soviets’ achieved their long-standing ambition of formal recognition of existing boundaries in Europe—that is, in the absence of a German peace treaty, acceptance by the West of the Soviets’ postwar gains and of the inviolability of their “bloc.” To be sure, they had to accept “basket three,” which committed them to respect human rights. They considered this pledge a mere formality, but it was one the East bloc dissidents would soon use to advance their cause by forming “Helsinki Watch Groups.” But this was a minor annoyance as against the great gain of international legitimation of their external empire.

zh: 与此同时，在美国于越南遭遇灾难之后，苏联人开始在第三世界展开新的扩张事业。赫鲁晓夫已经在埃及、印度、印度尼西亚、刚果以及稍有不同的古巴尝试过后殖民强权政治；但除古巴外，他的手段一直是外交支持和经济援助。在勃列日涅夫治下，渗透手段变成了军事力量，首先是古巴代理人在非洲，然后是苏联军队，如在阿富汗。这一进程始于1974年葡萄牙帝国的崩溃，它导致安哥拉内战；1976年，苏联的附庸在古巴军队帮助下击败了美国的附庸。次年，这一进程在埃塞俄比亚继续展开，美国的附庸海尔·塞拉西在古巴帮助下被苏联支持的革命政权“德格”击败。此后不久，苏联人跨过红海进入也门。
en: At the same time, and in the wake of the American disaster in Vietnam, the Soviets embarked on a new career of expansion in the Third World. Khrushchev had already tried his luck with postcolonial power politics in Egypt, India, Indonesia, the Congo, and, in a slightly different category, Cuba; but his means, except in Cuba, had been diplomatic support and economic aid. Under Brezhnev, the means of penetration became military might, first in the form of Cuban proxies in Africa and then in the form of Soviet troops, as in Afghanistan. The process started in 1974 with the collapse of the Portuguese empire, which led to a civil war in Angola; here the Soviet client defeated the American one with the help of Cuban troops in 1976. The process continued to unfold the next year in Ethiopia, where the American client Haile Selassie was defeated, again with Cuban help, by the Soviet-supported revolutionary Derg. And shortly thereafter, the Soviets crossed the Red Sea into Yemen.

zh: 但这场“危机之弧”——华盛顿当时这样称呼这些变化——很快延伸到阿富汗，而且恰逢反西方的伊朗革命。1978年，喀布尔一个倾向苏联的中立政权被阿富汗共产党中的一个派别推翻——似乎是由于当地主动。他们很快被一个更激进的派别取代，后者开始大张旗鼓地“建设社会主义”；这一政策激起了民族抵抗，威胁要彻底推翻共产主义。面对“社会主义征服被逆转”的可能性，莫斯科于1979年12月出兵干预，扶植一位较温和的共产党领导人巴布拉克·卡尔迈勒。干预的决定似乎不是由整个政治局作出的，而只是由四个人——勃列日涅夫、葛罗米柯、德米特里·乌斯季诺夫元帅和安德罗波夫——作出的。他们，或者至少曾驻布达佩斯的安德罗波夫，似乎还以匈牙利先例为参照，让卡尔迈勒扮演新卡达尔的角色。简言之，阿富汗干预并非像西方当时所想的那样出于地缘政治考虑，例如向中东石油推进一个突出部，而是出于一种衰老的意识形态关切：社会主义边疆不可侵犯。
en: But this “arc of crisis,” as these changes were called in Washington, soon extended into Afghanistan, and just at the moment of the anti-Western Iranian revolution. In 1978 a Soviet-leaning and neutralist regime in Kabul was overthrown—it seems on local initiative—by a faction of Afghan Communists. They were soon supplanted by a more radical faction that proceeded to “build socialism” with a vengeance; this policy fueled a national resistance that threatened to overthrow Communism entirely. Faced with the possibility of a “reversal of a conquest of socialism,” Moscow intervened with its own troops in December 1979 to install a more moderate Communist leader, Babrak Karmal. It seems that the decision to intervene was not taken by the full Politburo but by only four men—Brezhnev, Gromyko, Marshal Dmitri Ustinov, and Andropov. It also seems that they, or at least Andropov, a former minister to Budapest, thought in terms of the Hungarian precedent, with Karmal in the role of a new Kadar. In short, the Afghan intervention was not dictated by geopolitical considerations, such as advancing a salient toward Middle East oil, as the West thought at the time, but by a senescent ideological concern for the inviolability of the frontiers of socialism.

zh: 结果是缓和的终结。几个月前，卡特和勃列日涅夫还在维也纳以亲吻郑重确认的《第二阶段限制战略武器条约》，从未提交批准。与此同时，美国开始了一场大规模的全面军备建设，并将贯穿里根第一届政府。同一年，尼加拉瓜索摩查被推翻导致受卡斯特罗和莫斯科双方支持的桑地诺主义者胜利，国际气氛进一步恶化。看来尼加拉瓜现在将成为美洲的第二个古巴，并危及邻国萨尔瓦多。
en: The result was the end of détente. SALT II, which had been solemnly sealed with a kiss by Carter and Brezhnev only a few months earlier in Vienna, was never submitted for ratification. Concurrently, the United States began a major across-the-board arms buildup that would continue through the first Reagan administration. In that sarne year, the international atmosphere was further soured when the overthrow of Somoza in Nicaragua led to the triumph of the Sandinistas, who were supported by both Castro and Moscow. It seemed that Nicaragua would now become a second Cuba on the American continent and also endanger neighboring El Salvador.

zh: 但最严重的紧张新来源，是从1978年开始针对西欧部署的一种改进型中程弹道导弹——SS-20。
这种导弹的引入——它比前身射程更远，并携带多弹头——被解释为一种恐吓西欧人、从而在美国与其盟国之间制造裂痕、进而瓦解北约的企图。北约对SS-20的回应是计划在西欧部署美国潘兴II导弹和巡航导弹；这两种武器都将能够打到俄罗斯欧洲部分的主要城市中心。
en: But the most serious new source of tension was the deployment against Western Europe, beginning in 1978, of an improved intermediate-range ballistic missile, the SS-20.

The introduction of this missile—it had a longer range than its predecessor and carried multiple warheads-was interpreted as an effort to intimidate the Western Europeans and hence break up NATO by driving a wedge between the United States and its allies. NATO’s response to the SS-20 was a plan to deploy American Pershing II and cruise missiles in Western Europe; both of these weapons would be capable of reaching the major urban centers of European Russia.

zh: 到1981年里根总统任期开始时，所谓的欧洲导弹问题已成为一场重大实力考验。苏联人已经抢先一步，开始部署SS-20，而部署潘兴和巡航导弹还只是一个威胁。未能部署美国新武器将是西方的失败，而未能阻止其部署将是莫斯科的失败。于是接着发生了一场重大的意志较量，因为欧洲导弹问题的结果关系到全球力量平衡，特别是欧亚大陆的命运。冲突在1983年达到顶点：西德联邦议院批准部署潘兴导弹，苏联人作为回应，退出了他们一直与美国进行的中程核力量（INF）谈判。事情就这样僵持到1985年。
en: By 1981 and the beginning of Reagan’s presidency, the so-called Euromissile issue had become a major test of strength. The Soviets had stolen a march by having already begun the deployment of their SS-20s, while the deployment of the Pershings and the cruise was as yet only a threat. A failure to deploy the new American weapons would have been a defeat for the West, whereas a failure to block their deployment would have been a defeat for Moscow. A great contest of wills therefore ensued, for nothing less than the global balance of power, and in particular the fate of Eurasia, depended on the out-come of the Euromissiles issue. The conflict culminated in 1983 when the West German Bundestag approved deployment of the Pershings, and the Soviets, in answer, walked out of the INF (intermediate-range nuclear forces) negotiations they had been engaged in with the United States. And so matters remained stalemated until 1985.

zh: 尽管这场冲突确实是两个阵营之间的最重要的较量，但它是否像有时所说的那样构成一场“新”冷战，则不那么确定。毋宁说，1980年代初的冲突延续了可追溯到1948年的苏西关系基本模式，这一模式只被缓和短暂打断。因为冷战并不是轻率政策或基于相互无知的误解的产物，不是像缓和哲学所说的那样可以通过“建立信任措施”克服的。相反，正如苏联标准学说所说，它是两个“阵营”的利益和结构真正不相容的产物。从这个角度看，三四年的缓和是一种外交上的新经济政策，旨在为新的攻势积蓄苏联力量；而1975年后苏联重新施压的十年，则是回归制度的常态。
en: Although this conflict was indeed the supreme battle between the two camps, it is less certain that it constituted a “new” Cold War, as is sometimes alleged. Rather, the clash of the early eighties continued the basic pattern of Soviet-Western relations dating back to 1948, a pattern interrupted for only a brief time by détente. For the Cold War was not the product of rash policies or misunderstandings based on mutual ignorance that could be overcome by “confidence-building measures,” as the philosophy of détente had it. It was, rather, the product of the genuine incompatibility of the interests and structures of the two “camps,” as standard Soviet doctrine had it. In this perspective, the three or four years of détente were a kind of diplomatic NEP designed to build Soviet strength for a new offensive, and the ten years of renewed Soviet pressure after 1975 were a return to the system’s norm.

zh: 但这一回归——后来证明是制度在国际舞台上的最后一次逞强——也是对列宁主义革命冲动的漫画式模仿。因为世界头号社会主义国家、而且还是一个超级大国，竟在欧洲“帝国主义”的第三世界残骸中翻找安哥拉和阿富汗这样的战利品，如果不是那么悲惨，就近乎闹剧。马克思主义革命若要保持革命性，就注定要永久进行；因此，所谓的第二次冷战意味着为保持运动活力而不断推进革命这一必然要求，最终走进了死胡同。于是，在第三世界的每一个案例中，苏联人干预都是为了保卫一个他们不能放弃的马克思主义政权，否则就会丧失自己的革命信誉。但他们在每个案例中干预的方式都如此犬儒，所得又如此微不足道，以至于这种信誉还是丧失了；因此，整个制度被削弱而不是加强。
en: But this return, which turned out to be the system’s last international hurrah, was also a caricature of the Leninist revolutionary impulse. For the world’s premier socialist state, and a superpower to boot, to be rummaging in the Third World wreckage of European “imperialism” for such prizes as Angola and Afghanistan would be farcical were it not also so tragic. Marxist revolution is condemned to be permanent if it is to remain revolutionary, and therefore the so-called second Cold War represented the final cul-de-sac of the revolutionary necessity of constant advance to preserve the movement’s vigor. Thus, in each of these Third World cases, the Soviets intervened to defend a Marxist regime they could not abandon without forfeiting their own revolutionary credibility. But the manner in which they intervened in each case was so cynical, and the gain so derisory, that this credibility was forfeited anyway; thus, the system as a whole was undermined rather than strengthened.

zh: 1980年代初滑入危机，不仅是由于这种返祖式的意识形态反射，也是由于苏联制度此时已变成的军工复合体的惯性。因为在勃列日涅夫治下，党与军方的关系发生了重大变化，因为制度承担了为一场日益渺茫的未来胜利而进行无休止冷战的使命。这种变化了的关系还反映了一个事实：制度已变为由官名录而非领袖主导，从而给了军方更大的施压空间来提出自己的要求。
en: This slide into crisis of the early eighties was due not only to this atavistic ideological reflex, but also to the inertia of the military-industrial complex that the Soviet system had by now become. For under Brezhnev the relationship of the Party to the military had changed significantly because the system had assumed the mission of waging an endless Cold War for an increasingly improbable future victory. This changed relationship also reflected the fact that the system had come to be dominated by the
, not by the Leader, thereby giving the military greater leeway for pressing its demands.

zh: 这并不是说军方已成为西方意义上的“利益集团”，也不是说“制度多元主义”此时已成为制度的特征、党在各集团之间扮演裁判角色——这是勃列日涅夫时代西方广泛持有的一种观点。
军方继续通过官名录制度的交叉任职，作为党的一面发挥作用。但在该制度内部，它在纯政治领导层面前的分量，自斯大林或赫鲁晓夫时代以来已显著增加。
en: This is not to say that the military had become an “interest group” in the Western sense, and that “institutional pluralism” now characterized the system, with the Party playing the role of referee among the various groups—a perspective widely held in the West during the Brezhnev era.
The military continued to function as one face of the Party through the interlocking directorate of the
system. But within that system its weight with the strictly political leadership had increased notably since the time of Stalin or Khrushchev.

zh: 于是，1965年，勃列日涅夫的亲信安德烈·格列奇科元帅成为国防部长，更重要的是成为政治局委员。从那时起，在苏联历史上第一次，苏联军方首脑将进入最高决策机构。1974年，格列奇科的继任者是政治元帅德米特里·乌斯季诺夫，后者证明是军方利益更加热烈的代言人。因此，在1965—1985这二十年里，苏联军事预算的增长速度快于美国军事预算。而且，这种增长越来越推动制度把力量用于某种“目的”，即越来越多地进行不育却挑衅性的第三世界冒险，最后是部署SS-20导弹对付第一世界的心脏。
en: Thus in 1965 Brezhnev’s crony, Marshal Andrei Grechko, became minister of defense and, more importantly, a member of the Politburo. From this time onward, and for the first time in Soviet history, the head of the Soviet military would belong to the supreme decision-making body. In 1974 Grechko was succeeded by a political marshal, Dmitri Ustinov, who turned out to be an even more ardent spokesman for military interests. Thus for the twenty years 1965-1985 the Soviet military budget grew at a faster rate than that of the American military budget. And, more and more, this growth impelled the system to put its power to some “purpose” in increasingly sterile yet provocative Third World adventures, and, finally, to deploy the SS-20s against the heart of the First World.

en: INTERNAL ARTERIOSCLEROSIS

zh: 党与军方的逐步融合，与党与警察的融合同步进行。赫鲁晓夫曾大幅缩减克格勃的规模，并削弱其政治重要性，办法之一是始终不给其首脑政治局席位。但在1967年，即西尼亚夫斯基—丹尼尔审判之后，克格勃获得了新首脑和新地位：集体领导层任命尤里·安德罗波夫为该机构首脑。安德罗波夫是苏斯洛夫的门生，没有克格勃背景，被从中央委员会外事部门调来，担任整顿警察组织的任务；1969年，他成为政治局正式委员和政权最有影响力的人物之一。
en: The progressive melding of the Party with the military occurred

with the Party’s blending with the police. Khrushchev had greatly reduced the KGB’s size and diminished its political importance by, among other things, never giving its director a seat on the Politburo. But in 1967, after the Siniavskii-Daniel trial, the KGB received a new chief and a new status when the collective leadership installed Iurii Andropov as the agency’s director. A protégé of Suslov without a KGB background, Andropov was taken from the foreign section of the Central Committee and given the job of refurbishing the police organization; in 1969 he became a full member of the Politburo and one of the most influential figures of the regime.

children: 〔译注〕安德罗波夫1967年成为政治局候补委员，1973年才成为正式委员，原书所写1969年有误。
〔译注〕安德罗波夫1967年成为政治局候补委员，1973年才成为正式委员，原书所写1969年有误。

zh: 在安德罗波夫治下，克格勃大幅扩张；招募了受过更好教育的特工；并在莫斯科市中心捷尔任斯基广场旁建起一座宏伟的新附楼。安德罗波夫以比贝利亚更老练的方式运作，实现了该组织行动的现代化，并监督了一场恢复其威望的宣传运动。国外的情报搜集变得更加广泛和高效，国内一切公开的异见都被缓慢而有效地压制。与此同时，克格勃与党的关系发生了变化。斯大林曾用内务人民委员部统治党；勃列日涅夫和安德罗波夫则用克格勃与党一起统治社会（这当然也涉及克格勃对党本身的一定监视）。党和克格勃与军方一起，形成了三方交叉任职的权力结构。这就是“发达”或“成熟”社会主义的组织公式，是官名录党国的最终化身。
en: Under Andropov, the KGB was significantly expanded; better educated agents were recruited; and a grand new annex was built off Dzerzhinskii Square in central Moscow. Operating in a more sophisticated fashion than Beria had, Andropov modernized the organization’s operations and oversaw a propaganda campaign that restored its prestige. Intelligence-gathering abroad became more extensive and efficient, and at home all open dissidence was slowly but effectively suppressed. At the same time, the KGB’s relationship to the Party changed. Stalin had used the NKVD to govern the Party; Brezhnev and Andropov used the KGB to govern society in tandem with the Party (this, of course, also involved the KGB in some surveillance of the Party itself). And the Party and the KGB together functioned with the military in a kind of tripolar interlocking directorate. This was the organizational formula of “developed” or “mature” socialism, the final incarnation of the
Party-state.

zh: 克格勃地位再度上升的一个主要原因是持续存在的“异思者”（inakomyslyashchie）问题，即异见者。因为西尼亚夫斯基—丹尼尔审判并未达到让批评性知识分子闭嘴的目的；它只是刺激他们发展新的斗争技巧；其他异见者复制并分发了审判记录，这份记录最终在国外出版。
这份文件的编辑者于1967年被捕，而他们的审判又产生了新文件和在国外的进一步宣传。但异见也出现在政权的特权仆从中。1968年，安德烈·萨哈罗夫发表了他给领导层的信《论进步、自由与和平共处》，敦促结束审查制度并实现公共生活民主化。在他看来，这些步骤最终将通过东方社会主义经济形式与西方自由政治形式的“趋同”而结束冷战。
同年，独立的马克思主义历史学家罗伊·梅德韦杰夫通过地下出版渠道发表了《让历史审判》；在这部对斯大林时代的详细“揭露”中，他呼吁回归据称民主的列宁主义社会主义。
由于梅德韦杰夫不如其他人那样算得上异见者，他被允许在整个勃列日涅夫时代公开活动。
en: A principal reason for the KGB’s new prominence was the persistent problem of the

, “those-who-think-differently,” the dissidents. For the Siniavskii-Daniel trial had not achieved its purpose of silencing the critical intelligentsia; it had only stimulated them to develop new techniques of struggle; other dissidents reproduced and distributed a transcript of the trial that was eventually published abroad.

The editors of this document were arrested in 1967, and their trials, in turn, produced new documents and further international publicity. But dissidence also appeared among the privileged servants of the regime. In 1968 Andrei Sakharov published his letter to the leadership, “On Progress, Freedom, and Peaceful Co-existence,” in which he urged both the end of censorship and the democratization of public life. In his view, these steps would eventually lead to the end of the Cold War through a “convergence” of the socialist economic forms of the East with the liberal political forms of the West.
In that same year, the independent Marxist historian Roy Medvedev produced
; in this detailed “unmasking” of the Stalin era, he called for a return to an allegedly democratic Leninist socialism.
Because Medvedev was rather less of a dissident than were the others, he was allowed to function openly throughout the Brezhnev era.

zh: 萨哈罗夫和梅德韦杰夫以各自不同的方式，从下面推进了迄今为止只从上面推行的改革共产主义的种种版本。此外，他们的立场与布拉格之春期间实际实施的立场非常接近。但捷克改革运动被镇压，标志着可预见的未来内自上而下的苏联改革共产主义的终结，因此也导致允许自下而上的批评者持有的意见范围收窄。1969年，特瓦尔多夫斯基被解除《新世界》主编职务，这份苏联主要的自由主义刊物随之变得沉闷乏味。
en: In their different ways Sakharov and Medvedev were advancing from below versions of that Reform Communism that had hitherto come only from above. Moreover, their positions paralleled closely those actually being put into effect during the Prague Spring, But the crushing of the Czech reform movement marked the end of Soviet Reform Communism from above for the foreseeable future, and it therefore produced a narrowing of the range of opinion permitted to critics from below. In 1969 Tvardovskii was removed as editor of
, and this leading liberal Soviet publication lapsed into drabness.

zh: 尽管有这些挫折，异见仍在继续。1970年，萨哈罗夫和梅德韦杰夫连同物理学家瓦连京·图尔钦从体制内部发出一封致领导层的公开信，解释该国新近被承认的经济和技术落后，是缺乏思想自由和创造性思想遭到扼杀的结果。
在公开异见层面，弗拉基米尔·布科夫斯基等人采取的策略是，要求苏联政府遵守其纸面宪法的民主条文。
而在1975年《赫尔辛基协议》之后，这一方针导致在联盟各共和国建立赫尔辛基观察小组。此外，在整个勃列日涅夫时代，一个地下网络出版《当前事件纪事》——一份低调、严格按事实编目的记录，记载政权可资证明的违反自己法律的行为。
en: Despite these setbacks, dissidence continued. In 1970, from within the establishment itself, Sakharov and Medvedev, together with the physicist Valentin Turchin, released an open letter to the leadership explaining how the country’s newly recognized economic and technological backwardness was a result of the lack of intellectual freedom and the stifling of creative thought.
On the level of overt dissidence, such figures as Vladimir Bukovskii adopted the tactic of holding the Soviet government to the democratic letter of its paper constitution.

And, after the Helsinki Accords of 1975, this approach led to the creation of Helsinki Watch Groups in the various republics of the Union. In addition, throughout the Brezhnev era an underground network published a
—a low-key, strictly factual catalog of the regime’s documentable violations of its own laws.

zh: 然而，索尔仁尼琴仍然是最直言不讳的异见者，尽管他1963年后无法在俄国出版作品。他关于斯大林时代的两部小说于1960年代末在国外出版，然后在1974—1976年，他推出了《古拉格群岛》。当克格勃发现这份手稿时，索尔仁尼琴立即让人在国外出版了第一卷，由于这一违抗，他随即被强行押上飞机，流放国外。这一事件标志着政权对异见半容忍的终结。
en: Yet Solzhenitsyn remained the most vocal dissident, despite his inability to publish in Russia after 1963. Two of his novels on the Stalin era were published abroad in the late 1960s, and then, in 1974-1976, he produced

. When the KGB discovered this manuscript, Solzhenitsyn immediately had its first volume published abroad, and for this defiance he was forthwith forced aboard a plane and into foreign exile. This incident marked the end of the regime’s semitoleration of dissent.

〔译注〕《古拉格群岛》俄文第一卷于1973年12月在巴黎出版；索尔仁尼琴1974年2月被捕并驱逐出境。

zh: 但镇压比斯大林治下更为巧妙：主要人物像索尔仁尼琴一样未经正常审判便被驱逐出境；其他人被送进精神病“医院”；一些人被关押在彼尔姆43号这样的劳改营；更多的人只是被剥夺工作，或失去住房，或发现子女被禁止接受高等教育。1970年代末，非俄罗斯民族的文化领袖被有计划地从高加索、乌克兰和波罗的海国家流放。到本十年末，剩下的唯一著名异见者是萨哈罗夫。但在1980年，在批评入侵阿富汗之后，他被流放到高尔基市，大概是因为他掌握核机密，使政权无法把他送往国外。通过这一行动，克格勃有效压制了异见运动；赫鲁晓夫“头脑发热”的解冻后果终于被肃清。
en: But the repression was more subtle than it had been under Stalin: The principal figures were, like Solzhenitsyn, summarily exiled; others were consigned to psychiatric “hospitals”; some were incarcerated in labor camps such as Perm 43; many more were simply deprived of their jobs, or lost their housing, or found that their children were barred from higher education. In the late 1970s, cultural leaders of the non-Russian nationalities were systematically exiled from the Caucasus, Ukraine, and the Baltic states. By the end of the decade the only prominent dissident left was Sakharov. But in 1980, after criticizing the invasion of Afghanistan, he was exiled to the city of Gorky, presumably because his knowledge of nuclear secrets prevented the regime from sending him abroad. With this action the KGB effectively closed down the dissident movement; the consequences of Khrushchev’s “hare-brained” thaw had at last been liquidated.

zh: 但政权也摧毁了许多本可给它带来未来的才智之士，因为直到很晚，几乎所有这类异见者都仍留在改革共产主义的不与体制决裂的范围内。只有极少数人相信制度无法改革、因而必须被取代，安德烈·阿马尔里克1969年在《苏联能存活到1984年吗？》中阐述了这一观点。
尽管索尔仁尼琴在1970年代初以后不再相信制度本身可以改革，但即使他也只希望国家与社会之间实现职能分工，政治权力留给前者，言论自由归后者。
萨哈罗夫在被流放之前，也许甚至在改革时期的一段时间里，所想的仍是对制度进行广泛自由化和民主化，而不是取代它。当然，梅德韦杰夫只希望回到布哈林和新经济政策。诚然，如果最后这三个纲领得到实施，它们对苏联制度的破坏性将不亚于1968年改革对捷克斯洛伐克的破坏性。但重要的事实是，大多数苏联异见者没有意识到这一点，也没有清楚认识到制度的危机已有多么深重，即使晚至1970年代末也是如此。
en: But the regime had also destroyed many of the talents that alone could give it a future, for until very late almost all of these dissidents remained within the loyal bounds of Reform Communism. Only a very few believed that the system was incapable of reform and thus had to be replaced, a view that Andrei Amalrik expounded in 1969 in

en: And although Solzhenitsyn no longer believed after the early 1970s that the system as such was reformable, even he hoped for no more than a partition of functions between the state and society, with political power remaining with the former and freedom of expression going to the latter.
Sakharov until his exile, and perhaps even for a time under

, thought in terms of extensive liberalization and democratization of the system, not of its supersession. And Medvedev, of course, wanted only a return to Bukharin and the NEP. To be sure, had these last three programs been applied, they would have been as disruptive of the Soviet system as the 1968 reform was of Czechoslovakia’s. But the important fact is that most Soviet dissidents did not realize this or have any clear idea of how advanced the crisis of the system was, even as late as the end of the 1970s.

zh: 对于那些众多持部分批评意见的知识分子来说，这一点更加如此；他们仍然忠于制度，希望从内部改进它。这些人是苏联官方用语中所谓“知识分子”这一更大群体的一员，这个词只意味着受过某种技术或专业活动训练的人。自1930年代以来，俄国经历了一场教育革命，部分是为了传播“启蒙”，部分是为了形成新工业社会的干部。但这些人的思想大多是因循顺从的。苏联科学院各专业研究所的知识分子则完全不同，无论他们从事自然科学——如萨哈罗夫和图尔钦——还是从事较新的社会科学——如涅姆奇诺夫或阿甘别吉扬。
en: This was even more true of the numerous semicritical intellectuals who remained loyal to the system in the hope of improving it from within. These individuals were members of a much larger group known in official Soviet parlance as the “intelligentsia,” a term that simply meant people who had been trained for one or another kind of technical or professional activity. Since the 1930s, Russia had undergone an educational revolution, in part to spread “enlightenment” and in part to form the cadres of the new industrial society. But most of these people were conformist in their thinking. Quite different were the intellectuals of the specialized institutes of the Soviet Academy of Sciences, whether they worked in the natural sciences, as Sakharov and Turchin did, or in the newer social sciences, as did Nemchinov or Aganbegyan.

zh: 科学院的研究所网络在1960年代和1970年代大为扩展。

在莫斯科，最著名的例子是世界经济和国际关系研究所、美国和加拿大研究所、中央经济数学研究所。这些研究所的研究人员常常充当“顾问”（referents），在中央委员会书记处各部门起草立场文件。安德罗波夫在中央委员会工作时，网罗了这些研究所里一些最优秀、最聪明的人，其中许多人后来在改革时期崭露头角，包括戈尔巴乔夫的演讲撰稿人格奥尔基·沙赫纳扎罗夫和编辑费奥多尔·布尔拉茨基。1965年，在西伯利亚城市新西伯利亚，一个实际上相当于第二科学院的机构——比第一个更大胆、更具创新性——建立起来。在这些研究所或中央委员会工作的人显然不可能成为异见者而仍保住职位。但他们与异见文化有接触，并赞同其对制度的许多批评。
en: The Academy’s network of institutes had grown considerably in the 1960s and 1970s.

In Moscow the most prominent examples were the Institute of the World Economy and International Relations, the Institute of the USA and Canada, and the Central Economic-Mathematical Institute. Very often researchers from these institutes would work as “

,” drafting position papers in various sections of the Central Committee Secretariat. Andropov, when he was in the Central Committee, collected some of the best and the brightest of these institute men, and many of them later became prominent during

, including Gorbachev’s speechwriter, Georgii Shakhnazarov, and the editor Fedor Burlatskii. In 1965, in the Siberian city of Novosibirsk, a virtual second Academy—bolder and more innovative than the first—was created. People working in these institutes or in the Central Committee obviously could not become dissidents and still retain their posts. But they were in contact with dissident culture and shared many of its criticisms of the system.

zh: 同样，合法的苏联文学也受到从帕斯捷尔纳克到索尔仁尼琴的萨米兹达特作家的影响。

结果，社会主义现实主义的教规从未被正式否定，却在1960年代和1970年代缓慢受到侵蚀，哪怕只是为了让官方文学能与非法对手竞争。建设社会主义时代的英雄主题被放弃，一种在某种程度上涉及当下失望和不满的文学获准出现。特别是出现了一种“乡村文学”，赞美旧农民俄国的美德，哀叹其命运——这种文学间接批评了苏联刀耕火种式的发展方法，甚至批评了一般意义上的工业文明。当乡村作家开始鼓动反对污染时，这些文学变化最终逐渐转变为政治行动主义，贝加尔湖的特别案例就是如此。这种行动又与科学院各研究所中对苏联计划的一些批评有关。而这种零敲碎打的批评文化，隐含了对整个制度的批评，而批评者自己并不完全意识到这一含义。慢慢地，悄无声息地，制度的基本神话被侵蚀，人们越来越意识到这套谎言。
en: Similarly, legal Soviet literature was influenced by
writers, from Pasternak to Solzhenitsyn.

As a result, the canons of socialist realism, without ever being formally repudiated, were slowly eroded in the 1960s and 1970s, if only to permit official literature to compete with its illegal rival. The heroic themes of the days of building socialism were abandoned, and a literature that addressed in some measure the disappointments and discontents of the present was allowed to appear. In particular, there emerged a “village literature” celebrating the virtues, and bemoaning the fate, of old peasant Russia—a literature that was indirectly critical of Soviet slash-and-burn methods of development, and even of industrial civilization in general. These literary changes eventually shaded off into political activism when village writers took to agitating against pollution, as in the particular case of Lake Baikal. This agitation in turn had relevance for some of the critiques of Soviet planning that were heard in the Academy’s institutes. And this culture of piecemeal criticism implied a critique of the system taken as a whole, an implication that the critics themselves were not wholly aware of. Slowly, without fanfare, the basic myths of the system were being undermined and awareness of the Lie was coming closer to the surface of consciousness.

zh: 正是从所有这些来源——科学院各研究所、作家协会和电影工作者协会，甚至中央委员会工作人员——在勃列日涅夫、苏斯洛夫和安德罗波夫治下，出现了政权结构内部的影子异见。随着1970年代推移，这些圈子里习惯把知识分子分为“焦尔达诺·布鲁诺派”和“伽利略派”。前者是公开异见者，大胆直言，并因直言而落得悲惨下场；后者是隐蔽的批评者，公开赞同官方口号，私下却为一个新的解冻而努力——这些标签意味着第二条道路虽不那么英勇，却更有效。然而事实上，在勃列日涅夫治下，伽利略派最多只能声称自己偶尔能够防止最坏情况——让一位不谨慎的作家摆脱麻烦，或揭露一桩特别恶劣的腐败——但他们很少能够塑造政策。他们真正得到机会，要等到戈尔巴乔夫的改革。
en: It is from all of these sources—the Academy’s institutes, the Writers’ and Cinematographers’ Unions, and indeed the Central Committee staff—that a shadow dissidence within the regime’s structures emerged under Brezhnev, Suslov, and Andropov. As the decade of the seventies progressed, it became customary in such circles to divide the intelligentsia into the “Giordano Brunos” and the “Galileos.” The former were the overt dissidents who boldly spoke out and came to a bad end for their pains, whereas the latter were the closet critics who publicly subscribed to official slogans yet privately worked for a new thaw—the labels implying that the second course, though less heroic, was more effective. In fact, however, under Brezhnev the most the Galileos could claim was that they were occasionally able to prevent the worst—to get an imprudent writer out of trouble, or to expose a particularly egregious bit of corruption—but they were rarely able to mold policy. They would get their real chance only with Gorbachev’s

zh: 旧苏联秩序在末期以其庞大的体量沉重压在这个国家身上。赫鲁晓夫留给继任者的拥有一千一百万党员的党，到勃列日涅夫去世时已变成拥有一千九百万党员的党。

后一个数字约占近三亿人口的6%，在劳动年龄人口中占比更高。这些党员中有相当比例来自工人阶级和集体农庄农民。但绝大多数，约70%，来自经济、军队和知识职业的管理干部；而这个群体，由于其人数和技能，构成了党的重心。由于这些干部中较年长的一代大多出身“人民”，全党集会直到政权终结都保留着某种平民腔调。但到那时，把党说成工农组织已比以往更加没有意义，因为大多数年轻新党员来自“知识分子”。不过，“社会基础”并不是描述成熟政党的相关标准：重要的事实是，党囊括了国内每一个担任负责职位的人，而任何渴望这种职位的人都必须入党。
en: The old Soviet order at its end weighed on the country with an exceptional massiveness. The eleven-million-member Party that Khrushchev had bequeathed to his successors had by Brezhnev’s death become a nineteen-million-member Party.

The latter figure represented about 6 percent of a population of almost 300 million, and a much higher percentage of the working-age population. A respectable proportion of these members came from the working class and the kolkhoz peasantry. But the great majority, around 70 percent, were drawn from the managerial cadres in the economy, the military, and the intellectual professions; and this group, because of its numbers and its skills, constituted the center of gravity of the Party. Because most within the senior cohort of these cadres were originally from “the people,” all-Party gatherings retained a somewhat plebeian tone until the end of the regime. But by then it had become more meaningless than ever to speak of the Party as an organization of workers and peasants, since most of the younger recruits were largely from the “intelligentsia.” But “social base” is not a relevant criterion for characterizing the mature Party: the important facts are that the Party included everyone in the country who held a position of responsibility, and that anyone who aspired to such a position had to join.

zh: 这样的党不可能是一个狂热分子或有坚定信念的意识形态者的组织。尽管如此，其成员都深受灌输。他们所有人都必须缴纳党费，参加小组会议讨论最新的党指示，并且都必须跟上党的报刊，以便向别人解释当前路线。因此，对大多数党员来说，一定程度的“党性”（partiinost）即使不是信念，至少也已成为根深蒂固的习惯。他们所有人都因长期沉浸于党特有的“木头语言”而受到影响。的确，党那种语言统治式的“新话”，即索尔仁尼琴所说的谎言的语言，是维系整个制度的主要力量。因此，直到1980年代接近尾声，政权仍雇用数万名“鼓动员”，花费数十亿卢布，把1920年代列宁主义那些如今几乎毫无生气的范畴灌输到民众头脑中，尤其是灌输到其“先锋队”即党的头脑中。
en: Such a Party could not be an organization of zealots or committed ideologues. Nonetheless, its members were well-indoctrinated. All of them had to pay dues and attend cell meetings to discuss the latest Party directive, and they all had to keep up with the Party press in order to explain the current line to others. Thus, for most members a degree of “Party-mindedness” (

) had become, if not a matter of conviction, at least an ingrained habit. They were all influenced by their constant immersion in the Party’s special “wooden language.” Indeed, the Party’s logocratic “newspeak,” the language of the Lie, as Solzhenitsyn called it, was a major force in holding the whole system together. Thus the regime, until almost the end of the 1980s, employed tens of thousands of “agitators” and spent billions of rubles to din the now almost lifeless categories of the Leninist 1920s into the minds of the population, and above all into its “avant-garde,” the Party.

zh: 因此，制度的宣传鼓动继续把现实简化为“阶级立场”、普遍“斗争”以及“社会主义”对“帝国主义”的重大二分法。亚历山大·季诺维耶夫曾是中央委员会的学术顾问，1970年代末从影子异见转向公开异见，他一直是党的超现实语言的重要分析者，讽刺赫鲁晓夫的“光辉未来”以及勃列日涅夫同样虚幻的“现实社会主义”。尽管如此，他也承认“意识形态影响的强大磁场”具有不可逃避的性质。
en: Thus the system’s agitprop continued to reduce reality to “class positions,” universal “struggle,” and the great dichotomy of “socialism” versus “imperialism.” Aleksandr Zinoviev, an academic consultant to the Central Committee who went from shadow to overt dissidence in the late 1970s, has been the great analyst of the surreal language of the Party, satirizing Khrushchev’s “radiant future” as well as Brezhnev’s equally phantom “real socialism.” Nonetheless, he has also recognized the inescapable character of the “powerful magnetic field of ideological influence.”

zh: 至少在一个层面上情况如此：在这个层面上，没有人敢于公开质疑意识形态。但在另一个层面上，党员以务实、自利的方式经营自己的事业，这种情况削弱了他们的公开意识形态立场。尽管如此，在这个群众性政党中，其成员受到萨米兹达特文学和生活日益专业化的影响，思想的意识形态外衣越来越薄。认为对一千九百万人、对所有问题都存在唯一“正确”立场的信念，日益显得难以置信——尤其是因为党的知识分子已经读过亚历山大·季诺维耶夫和索尔仁尼琴，甚至康奎斯特。
en: At least this was the situation on one level, where no one dared question the ideology in public. But on another level Party members went about their careers in a pragmatic, self-interested fashion, and this circumstance undercut their public ideological stance. Still, in this mass Party, with its members influenced by

literature and the growing professionalization of life, the ideological veneer of thought was wearing increasingly thin, The belief that there was a single “correct” position for nineteen million people and on all questions was on the point of appearing implausible—all the more so because the Party intellectuals had read Aleksandr Zinoviev and Solzhenitsyn, and even Conquest.

zh: 这一群众性政党的凝聚力受到侵蚀，组织与社会结构关系的变化又加剧了这一过程。1930年代和1940年代，国家生活在永久紧急状态中，首先是因为建设社会主义的内部战争，然后是因为对德国的外部战争。在这种情况下，一个军事型政党从上面强制动员社会全部资源具有一定的“合理性”，因此斯大林那个拥有一两百万党员的党有力地履行了领导者角色。但在1945年胜利后，国家安定下来，进入一个没有战争或严重战争威胁的长期模式化增长过程。在任何其他制度下，这种情况都意味着回归常态，但党按其本性无法完成这样的转变：它的全部存在理由就是指挥和领导，以保持其对权力的垄断。因此，它继续把自己的本性强加于社会，而不是使自己顺应社会变化的需要。但它此时这样做，不是通过暴力强制，而是通过常规和惯性。
en: The erosion of the mass Party’s cohesion was furthered by changes in the organization’s structural relation to society. In the 1930s and 1940s the country lived in a permanent state of emergency, first because of the internal war to build socialism and then because of the external war against Germany. Under such circumstances it made a certain “sense” for a military-type Party to mobilize coercively all of society’s resources from above, and so Stalin’s one- to two-million-member Party vigorously exercised its role as leader. But after the victory of 1945, the country settled down to a long process of patterned growth without war or serious threat of war. Under any other system these circumstances would have meant a return to normality, but the Party, by its very nature, was unable to accomplish such a transformation: its whole raison d’être was to command and lead in order to preserve its monopoly of power. Thus it continued to impose its nature on society rather than bend itself to the changing needs of society. But it did so now not by a violent wrench but by routine and inertia.

zh: 因此，从1950年代到1980年代初，党继续监督和管理社会的一切活动；由于这些活动在数量和复杂性上不断增加，党的规模也不断扩大——也日益臃肿——以便掌控一切。结果是官僚机构空前膨胀。如前所述，1960年代的45个工业部又增加了其他领域的25个部，到1980年代共有70个经济部；莫斯科市中心的越来越多建筑，无论新旧，都被政府工作人员占据。
在农村，集体农庄和国营农场又滋生了约三百万官僚。整个制度的决策机关，即老广场上的中央委员会书记处，同街那头的克格勃一样，办公规模和人员数量都不断扩大。所有大型企业都有党委，每个机构都有党的支部。对中央委员会负责的政治军官监督军队，而同样是党员的克格勃特工监督所有人。于是，所有负责职位都由党员填补，而党员队伍此时已达一千九百万。
en: Hence, from the 1950s to the early 1980s the Party continued to monitor and manage all of society’s activities; and since these activities constantly increased in number and complexity, the Party constantly grew in size—and cumbersomeness—in order to stay on top of everything. The result was an unprecedented bureaucratic hypertrophy. As already noted, to the forty-five industrial ministries in the 1960s were added twenty-five in other fields, for a total of seventy economic ministries by the 1980s; and more and more of central Moscow’s buildings, old and new, were taken over by government staffs.

In the countryside the collective farms and state farms spawned some three million additional bureaucrats. The policymaking organ for the whole system, the Central Committee Secretariat on Old Square, grew in physical size and in the number of effectives, just like the KGB down the street. Party committees existed in all large enterprises, and every institution had its Party cell. Political officers responsible to the Central Committee monitored the military, and the KGB’s agents, who were also Party members, monitored everybody. And so all positions of responsibility came to be filled by Party members, whose ranks now counted nineteen million.

zh: 因此，党以其各种身份之一直接介入社会的每一项职能活动，这是一个新进展。当然，党一直领导和指挥一切重要事务，但在1960年代和1970年代，它开始实际指导大多数事情本身。列宁发明的双重行政体制此时被推到了极限。为承认这一新情况，1977年勃列日涅夫以一份新的根本文件取代1936年斯大林宪法，其主要创新是第六条。该条款第一次正式承认，党在社会中行使“领导和指导作用”。
en: Thus the Party, in one or another of its guises, became directly involved in every functional activity in society, and this was a new development. The Party, of course, had always led and commanded in all essential matters, but in the 1960s and 1970s it took to actually directing most things itself. The system of dual administration invented by Lenin was now pushed to its ultimate limit. In recognition of this new state of affairs, in 1977 Brezhnev replaced the Stalin Constitution of 1936 with a new fundamental document in which the principal innovation was Article VI. This provision formally recognized for the first time that the “leading and governing role” in society was exercised by the Party.

en: But, of course, a Party of such size cannot lead unless it is itself led. The great mass of Party members who held functional positions in society received their directives from the full-time Party workers of the apparat—or, in Orwell’s terminology, the Inner Party governed the Outer Party, while the latter acted as the system’s representative in the workplaces of society. Although some measure of privilege and prestige accrued to all Party members, real power and significant perquisites were reserved for the full-time apparat; and this group, together with the key governmental, economic, and military cadres, formed the

根据他的数字，这个群体约有七十五万人；连同家属，也许总共近三百万人。即使有些估计更高，在如此庞大的国家里，这仍是一个小群体，却掌握如此巨大的权力而不受问责。尽管党在勃列日涅夫治下拥有威风的“领导和指导作用”，它实际上正在变成一个脆弱的乳齿象。随着意识形态力量衰退，由有能力的专业人员组成的外党越来越不敬畏往往无能的意识形态管理者的内党。广大民众不再期待“光辉未来”，越来越憎恨官名录的特权和腐败。有技能、有能力、有抱负的人，越来越被一个自我任命、唯一职能就是行使“领导作用”的组织的无处不在的代表和无所不在的宣传鼓动所挫败。事实上，官名录共产主义的群众性政党指挥一切，却什么也不生产，因此像寄生虫一样寄生在国家机体上。但同样，它正在毁掉自己赖以寄生的根基。

dates back to the 1930s, but the world became aware of it only in 1980 through Mikhail Voslenskii’s book of the same name.

According to his figures, this group numbered about three quarters of a million people; together with their families, it perhaps totaled nearly three million. While other estimates are even higher, this was still a small group to wield so much power without accountability in such a huge country. Despite the Party’s imposing “leading and governing role” under Brezhnev, it was in fact becoming a fragile mastodon. With the force of ideology on the wane, the Outer Party of competent professionals was less and less awed by the Inner Party of often incompetent ideological administrators. The population at large no longer expected a “radiant future” and increasingly resented the perquisites and corruption of the

. And people of skill, competence, and ambition were increasingly frustrated by the omnipresent representatives and the ubiquitous agitprop of a self-appointed organization whose only function was to exercise its “leading role.” And, in fact, the mass Party of
Communism commanded everything yet produced nothing, and so lived like a parasite on the body of the nation. But by the same token, it was destroying the very substance on which it fed.

zh: 最薄弱的环节：外部帝国
en: THE WEAKEST LINK: THE EXTERNAL EMPIRE

zh: 当苏维埃主义的内帝国走向死胡同时，外部帝国正越过改革共产主义，走向真正退出制度。的确，勃列日涅夫时代最重大的事件不是发生在苏联本身，而是发生在东欧——先是1968年的捷克斯洛伐克，然后是1980—1981年的波兰。这些事件之所以更加重要，是因为在中国已经脱离这一阵营之后，东欧卫星国是“世界社会主义体系”仍是一支统一的力量的最明显标志。
en: While the Inner Empire of Sovietism was approaching a dead end, the External Empire was moving beyond Reform Communism towards an actual exit from the system. Indeed, the most significant events of the Brezhnev era took place not in the Soviet Union itself but in Eastern Europe—first in Czechoslovakia in 1968, and then in Poland in 1980-1981. These events were all the more important because, with China in secession, the East European satellites were the most palpable indication that the “world socialist system” was still a coherent force.

zh: 1968年的布拉格之春是后斯大林时代最深入的改革共产主义尝试，因此它的失败最能揭示任何此类努力的内在矛盾。捷克斯洛伐克改革始于一种迟来的去斯大林化尝试，类似于赫鲁晓夫治下其他地方发生的情况。当地党的领袖安东宁·诺沃提尼设法把去斯大林化推迟了十年，结果只是加剧了党内和国内的挫折感。为打破这一僵局，1967年底勃列日涅夫推了他一把，把他赶下台，捷克改革派扶植了亚历山大·杜布切克。这些改革派与1956年的赫鲁晓夫不同，有一个准备充分、范围广泛的纲领；此外，他们在一个准备并渴望彻底变革的国家里运作。
en: The Prague Spring of 1968 was the most far-reaching attempt at Reform Communism of the post-Stalin era, and for this reason its failure was the most revealing regarding the inner contradictions of any such effort. The Czechoslovak reform began as a belated attempt at the sort of de-Stalinization that had occurred elsewhere under Khrushchev. The local Party leader, Antonin Novotny, had managed to defer de-Stalinization for a decade, thereby only aggravating frustration within the Party and the country. To unfreeze this situation, in late 1967 Brezhnev gave him a shove from office, and the Czech reformers installed Alexander Dubcek. These reformers, unlike Khrushchev in 1956, had a well-prepared and wide-ranging program; in addition, they were operating in a country ready and eager for thoroughgoing change.

〔译注〕诺沃提尼于1968年1月被杜布切克接任第一书记。勃列日涅夫1967年12月访捷时没有按诺沃提尼的期望公开支持他，但将这一变化简化为勃列日涅夫当年直接将其赶下台并不准确。

zh: 捷克改革派借鉴南斯拉夫经验以及西方关于现代化的文献，像所有东欧前辈一样寻求“通往社会主义的独特道路”；在捷克的情况下，这意味着一条适应其社会先进性质的道路。

他们的愿望体现在1968年4月的党的《行动纲领》中，后来概括为“人道面孔的社会主义”这一口号。改革派论证说，既然通向社会主义的阶级斗争已经获胜，社会中的各种利益就应被允许组织自己的机构，甚至进行政治竞争。而在接下来的几个月里，独立的自愿组织和具有政党雏形的团体确实出现了。但这种新兴的社会多元主义也需要“社会主义法治”，尤其是结束审查制度，因为自由是发达经济所需的文化和科学创造力的前提。然而与此同时，改革派重申了“党的领导作用”原则，却没有面对这一作用如何能与言论和结社自由相协调的问题。当然，这一点最终毁了这场实验。
en: Drawing on the Yugoslav experience, as well as on Western literature about modernization, the Czech reformers, like all of their East European predecessors, sought a “separate road to socialism”; in the Czech’s case, this meant a road adapted to the advanced nature of their society.

Their aspirations were set forth in the Party’s Action Program of April 1968 and later summarized in the slogan “socialism with, a human face.” Since the class struggle leading to socialism had already been won, the reformers argued, the various interests in society should be allowed to organize their own institutions and even to compete politically. And indeed in the next months independent voluntary associations and protopolitical parties appeared. But this emerging social pluralism also required a “socialist rule of law,” and especially the end of censorship, since freedom was a prerequisite of the cultural and scientific creativity required by a developed economy. At the same time, however, the reformers reaffirmed the principle of the “leading role of the Party” without facing the problem of how that role could be reconciled with freedom of expression and association. And this, of course, would do the experiment in.

zh: 党的经济纲领几乎与政治纲领一样不正统，它出自奥塔·希克之手。这是柯西金改革的更大胆版本，要求给予经理层相当大的自主权，把利润作为计划的一个组成部分或“指标”，并为低效单位可能破产作出规定。工人委员会将被选举产生，并参与工厂管理，这一措施让人想起南斯拉夫改革和1917年俄国的“工人监督”。因此，该纲领把工业新经济政策与一种无政府工团主义和文化多元主义结合起来，后者被视为经济发展的刺激因素。
en: Almost as unorthodox as its political program was the Party’s economic program, the work of Ota Sik. A bolder version of the Kosygin reforms, it called for a significant measure of managerial autonomy, the use of profit as an integral component or “indicator” of the Plan, and provision for the possibility that inefficient units might go bankrupt. Workers’ councils were to be elected and given a share in plant management, a measure reminiscent of the Yugoslav reforms and of “workers’ control” in Russia during 1917. The program thus combined an industrial NEP with a form of anarcho-syndicalism, as well as cultural pluralism, the latter viewed as a stimulus to economic development.

zh: 长期以来，人们理所当然地认为这一纲领既有前途又切实可行，如果得到贯彻，最终将通向资本主义与社会主义之间著名的“第三条道路”。改革运动仅仅八个月后就被苏联干预切断，因此被视为一场悲剧。毫无疑问，布拉格之春是后斯大林几十年里满怀抒情希望的重大时刻：当时东方和西方都有许多人把它视为苏联式现代化迟来的回报，视为冷战可能以资本主义与共产主义的某种趋同而结束的迹象。这一事件确实是悲剧性的。
en: It was long taken as axiomatic that this program was both promising and practical, and that if followed it would at last have led to the famous “third way” between capitalism and socialism. That the reform movement was cut off by Soviet intervention after only eight months thus has been considered a tragedy. No doubt the Prague Spring was the great lyrical moment of hope during the post-Stalin decades: in both the East and the West, many saw it at the time as the belated payoff of Soviet-style modernization and a sign that the Cold War might end with some sort of convergence of capitalism and Communism. And the event was indeed tragic.

zh: 然而，悲剧不在于某个错失的机会，而在于布拉格版本的改革共产主义在本质上不可能实现。问题的一部分在于纲领本身的内容：走向利润和真实价格的举措，被这些“指标”继续服从指令性计划所抵消；而言论和结社自由则受制于党对其领导作用的坚持。然而，捷克领导人像他们之前的其他改革共产主义者一样，完全没有意识到存在任何此类矛盾；这种缺乏自觉源于改革派的心理。
en: The tragedy, however, lay not in some missed opportunity but in the intrinsic impossibility of realizing the Prague version of Reform Communism. A part of the problem was the content of the program itself: the move towards profit and real prices was counteracted by the continued subordination of these “indicators” to a directive Plan, while freedom of speech and association were subject to the Party’s insistence on its leading role. Yet the Czech leaders, like other Reform Communists before them, were quite unaware that any such contradictions existed; and this unawareness was a consequence of the reformers’ psychology.

zh: 为了采取任何行动，改革派必须相信改革是可能的，因此制度是可塑的。他们之所以产生这种信念，部分是因为改革共产主义在1968年还相对年轻：赫鲁晓夫的下台似乎并不标志着变革的终结，因为他的解冻动力仍存在于柯西金的政策中，也存在于忠诚却批判的苏联知识分子的活动中。此外，捷克改革派的乐观主义还得到他们自己意识形态预设的加强。
en: In order to take any action, the reformers had to believe that reform was possible and that the system, therefore, was malleable. They were encouraged in this belief in part by Reform Communism’s relative youth in 1968: Khrushchev’s fall did not appear to mark the end of change because the impetus of his thaw was still present in the policies of Kosygin and in the activities of a loyal yet critical Soviet intelligentsia. Moreover, the Czech reformers’ optimism was reinforced by their own ideological presuppositions.

zh: 改革派从制度是可能的社会组织“最高”形式这一前提出发，无法设想放弃它。然而从经验上，他们知道现有状态的制度在很大程度上否定了自己的理想。既然按定义这种缺陷不可能是最高制度的过错，那就只能是某种偶然力量造成的意外，这种力量叫“斯大林主义”。因此，解决办法是通过制定政策，使最高制度回归某种叫“真正的列宁主义”或“人道面孔的社会主义”的东西，从而清除这个异物。但在诉诸这些对共产主义原则的迂回变体时，布拉格改革派实际上承认了他们渴望改变的制度的各项主张的有效性；因此，即使他们在实施与那种逻辑相矛盾的措施，他们仍然是其逻辑的囚徒。
en: Starting from the premise that the system was the “highest” possible form of social organization, the reformers could not conceive of abandoning it. Yet empirically, they knew that the system in its existing state largely negated its own ideals. Since by definition this defect could not be the fault of the highest system, it had to be an accident due to an adventitious force called “Stalinism.” The solution, therefore, was to purge the highest system of this alien body by devising policies that would return it to something called “true Leninism” or “socialism with a human face.” But in resorting to these circumlocutory variations on Communist principles, the Prague reformers were in fact acknowledging the validity of the claims of the system they aspired to change; they thus remained prisoners of its logic even as they were implementing measures that contradicted that logic.

zh: 他们困境的悲剧如下：如果他们更清醒，要么根本无法行动，那样就会在绝望中放弃；要么就必须尝试一场革命，那样就会走向失败。因此，他们不得不凭信念相信第三条道路确实存在，半自欺地相信他们并没有在摧毁制度，并希望自己能骗莫斯科也相信同样的事。但莫斯科当时正刚从自己对后斯大林之春的幻想中清醒过来；于是杜布切克及其同事梦游般地走向了“勃列日涅夫主义”加诸他们的毁灭。
en: The tragedy of their dilemma was as follows: Had they been more lucid, either they would have been unable to act at all, in which case they would have given up in despair, or they would have had to attempt a revolution, in which case they would have gone down to defeat. Therefore, they had to take it on faith that the third way did exist, half-fooling themselves into believing that they were not destroying the system and hoping they could fool Moscow into believing the same thing. But Moscow at the time was recovering from its own illusions of a post-Stalinist spring; thus Dubcek and his colleagues sleepwalked to their doom at the hands of the “Brezhnev doctrine.”

zh: 促成危机爆发的是这样一个事实：到1968年夏天，捷克斯洛伐克的制度已在大步走向解体。6月，一群知识分子发表宣言——《两千字宣言》——呼吁人民把自由化进程掌握在自己手中，而不再听任党掌控。到8月，党本身已颁布新党章，使其内部结构民主化：选举将采用无记名投票，对领导人任职年数加以限制；此外，党内团体被允许组织为派别，这违反了列宁1921年制定的党的统一规则。由于这些章程是在为下个月党代会做准备时公布的，在勃列日涅夫及其同事看来，它们预示着制度的自我清算。东德的瓦尔特·乌布利希和波兰的哥穆尔卡考虑到自己政权的脆弱，对这场即将到来的“反革命”谴责得更加激烈。
en: What precipitated the crisis was the fact that the system in Czechoslovakia was well on its way to unravelling by the summer of 1968. In June a group of intellectuals issued a proclamation—the “2000 words”—calling on the people to take the process of liberalization into their own hands and away from the Party. By August the Party itself had issued new statutes democratizing its internal structure: Elections were to be by secret ballot, and a limitation was placed on the number of years leaders could hold office; moreover, groups within the Party were allowed to organize as factions in violation of the rule on Party unity that Lenin had set in 1921. Since these statutes had been published in anticipation of a Party Congress the following month, they seemed to Brezhnev and his colleagues to presage the system’s self-liquidation. East Germany’s Walter Ulbricht and Poland’s Gomulka, mindful of the fragility of their own regimes, were even more vehement in their denunciation of this impending “counterrevolution.”

zh: 所有这些第一书记的诊断都是正确的：在短短八个月里，自由化的风潮以异常速度从党的改革派蔓延到知识分子，最后蔓延到工人；整个国家的民众想要一种仍可称为共产主义、但党实际上将变得多余的新秩序。如果党的控制权在布拉格崩溃，它还能在华沙和柏林维持多久？或者最终甚至在莫斯科维持多久？
en: And all of these First Secretaries were correct in their diagnosis: In a mere eight months the contagion of liberalization had spread with extraordinary rapidity from the reform wing of the Party to the intellectuals, and finally to the workers; the whole nation wanted a new order that it could still call Communist but in which the Party would in fact be superfluous. And if the Party’s control collapsed in Prague, how long could it be maintained in Warsaw and Berlin? Or, eventually, even in Moscow?

zh: 尽管如此，干预布拉格将比1956年干预布达佩斯更困难，当时一场公开的起义使苏联人相对容易地为使用武力辩护。但在布拉格，一个共产党政府仍在掌权，并继续宣称忠于华沙条约。因此，8月21日的干预不是苏联的单方面行动，而是“兄弟的”华沙条约组织应忠诚的捷克共产党人呼吁而名义上采取的行动。尽管这次行动在军事上是组织杰作，在政治上却是失败：捷克领导层不仅拒绝使其合法化，而且捷克反对派也无法产生一个卡达尔来取代杜布切克。于是，在这场戏剧的超现实结局中，领导层被绑架到莫斯科，被迫撤销其纲领，然后被恢复名义上的权力，而有关各方则继续假装同志般地团结在社会主义价值观之下。
en: Still, an intervention in Prague would be more difficult than the one in Budapest in 1956, when an outright revolt had made it relatively easy for the Soviets to justify the use of force. But a Communist government was still in control in Prague, and it continued to proclaim its fidelity to the Warsaw Pact. Hence, the intervention of August 21 was not a unilateral Soviet action but the nominal undertaking of the “fraternal” Warsaw Pact in response to an appeal from loyal Czech Communists. Although militarily the operation was a masterpiece of organization, politically it was a failure: not only did the Czech leadership refuse to legitimate it, but the Czech opposition could not produce a Kadar to take Dubcek’s place. So, in the surreal conclusion to the drama, the leadership was abducted to Moscow, forced to rescind its program, and then restored to nominal power, while all concerned kept up the pretense of comradely communion in socialist values.

zh: 在这一门面背后，苏联人及其正统捷克盟友着手进行他们所谓的局势“正常化”。勃列日涅夫回应布拉格改革派创造“人道面孔的社会主义”的僭越，回收了铁托的旧口号，宣布捷克人已经享有“现实存在的社会主义”；这一称谓从此在所有兄弟国家成为正统。具体而言，这意味着清算春天的一切痕迹，并清洗全国三分之一的党员。到1969年初，正常化已进展到足以用一位想当捷克卡达尔的人古斯塔夫·胡萨克取代杜布切克；胡萨克像他的匈牙利前任一样，曾在斯大林治下被监禁；胡萨克将掌权到1988年。至于杜布切克，直到1989年制度崩溃，他都相信干预是一场本可避免的错误，而一种改良的共产主义仍是该国问题的真正答案。
en: Behind this facade, the Soviets and their orthodox Czech allies proceeded with what they called the “normalization” of the situation. Brezhnev answered the Prague reformers’ presumption to create “socialism with a human face” by recycling Tito’s old slogan to declare that the Czechs already enjoyed “really existing socialism”; and this designation was henceforth canonical in all of the fraternal countries. Concretely, this meant the liquidation of all vestiges of the Spring and the purge of a third of the national Party. By early 1969, normalization was sufficiently advanced to replace Dubcek with a would-be Czechoslovak Kadar, Gustav Husak, who, like his Hungarian predecessor, had been imprisoned under Stalin; Husak would remain in power until 1988. As for Dubcek, until the very collapse of the system in 1989, he believed that the intervention had been an avoidable error and that an improved Communism remained the real answer to the country’s problems.

children: 〔译注〕胡萨克于1987年12月卸任捷共总书记，1989年12月辞去共和国总统职务；两项离职时间不同于原书所写的1988年。
〔译注〕胡萨克于1987年12月卸任捷共总书记，1989年12月辞去共和国总统职务；两项离职时间不同于原书所写的1988年。

zh: 然而，对苏联人及其盟友来说，干预是一个基本原则问题，体现在很快被称为“勃列日涅夫主义”的东西中。这一主义认为，虽然捷克人有权选择自己的社会主义道路，但他们错误的政策实际上威胁到社会主义在国内和所有“兄弟”国家的存在。因此，干预不是西方看来那样的赤裸裸权力行使，而是一种正当的自卫措施。本质上，该主义断言社会主义不可分割，而社会主义“真实存在”的标准是“党的领导作用”。因为社会主义党国的国际团结，对各地意识形态专制的党治政体的生存至关重要。团结之所以至关重要，首先有一个形而上学理由：在一个合法性源于历史逻辑的运动中，“社会主义的成果”一经取得就必须是“不可逆转的”，否则制度就会被揭穿为伪科学的骗局。社会主义团结还有一个现实理由：让各地共产党统治下的民众保持恐惧，从而保持被动；因为如果一个被囚禁的民族证明逃脱实际上是可能的，那么其他民族也会找到逃脱的勇气。
en: For the Soviets and their allies, however, the intervention was a matter of basic principle, embodied in what soon became known as the “Brezhnev doctrine.” This doctrine held that although the Czechs had a right to choose their own road to socialism, their misguided policies in fact threatened the existence of socialism at home and in all “fraternal” countries. Thus, the intervention was not an exercise of raw power—as it appeared to the West—but a legitimate measure of self-defense. In essence, the doctrine asserted that socialism was indivisible and that the criterion of socialism’s “real existence” was the “leading role of the Party.” For the international solidarity of socialist Party-states was vital for the survival of ideocratic partocracy everywhere. Solidarity was vital first for a metaphysical reason: in a movement where legitimacy derived from the logic of history, the “conquests of socialism,” once made, had to be “irreversible” or the system would be unmasked as a pseudoscientific fraud. And socialist solidarity was also necessary for a practical reason; to keep the Communist populations everywhere afraid and therefore passive; for if one captive nation demonstrated that escape was in fact possible, then others would also find the courage to escape.

zh: 但捷克斯洛伐克领导层也误解了制度的另一个方面。捷克人记得匈牙利人退出华沙条约的错误，因此坚持自己对那个组织的忠诚，仿佛莫斯科受到的威胁主要不是来自他们的“反革命”榜样，而是来自其军事缓冲地带的缩小。莫斯科首要关切是意识形态的，这一点可以通过考察尼古拉·齐奥塞斯库治下的罗马尼亚得到证实。在布拉格之春那一年，罗马尼亚不仅通过与毛泽东和戴高乐这样形形色色的领导人交好而背离莫斯科的外交政策，实际上还停止参加华沙条约，办法之一就是拒绝与华约一起干预捷克斯洛伐克。然而与此同时，齐奥塞斯库在国内实行最正统的共产主义秩序，因此除了莫斯科的皱眉之外，从未遭受任何更严重的后果。
en: But the Czechoslovak leadership misunderstood another aspect of the system as well. Remembering the mistake of the Hungarians in withdrawing from the Warsaw Pact, the Czechs had insisted on their own loyalty to that organization, as if Moscow were not far more threatened by their “counterrevolutionary” example than by diminution of its military glacis. That Moscow’s primary concern was ideological is borne out by considering Romania under Nicolae Ceausescu. In the year of the Prague Spring, Romania not only broke with Moscow’s foreign policy by courting leaders as diverse as Mao and de Gaulle, she in effect also ceased to participate in the Warsaw Pact by, among other things, refusing to join it in the Czechoslovak intervention. Yet at the same time, Ceausescu enforced the most orthodox Communist order at home and so never suffered anything more than frowns from Moscow.
