〔译注〕罗马尼亚拒绝参加1968年入侵，并限制参与部分联合军事活动，但并未退出华约；其后仍参加华约政治协商，双方常有分歧。

zh: 勃列日涅夫认为捷克斯洛伐克的偏离者更加危险，这并没有错。既然按定义永远不可能有任何东西比“现实社会主义”更好或更高，那么外部帝国中对改革共产主义最认真的一次尝试就必须以外科手术式干预来终结。同样，赫鲁晓夫去斯大林化的动力终于在东欧人此时称为“老大哥”的国家里被制止，完全勃列日涅夫式的“停滞”时代开始了。
en: And Brezhnev was not mistaken in considering the Czechoslovaks the more dangerous deviationists. Since by definition there could never be anything better or higher than “real socialism,” the most serious attempt ever at Reform Communism in the External Empire had to be ended by surgical intervention. By the same token, the impetus of Khrushchev’s de-Stalinization was at last halted in the country that East Europeans now called Big Brother, and the age of full Brezhnevite “stagnation” began.

zh: 1968年也标志着共产主义在匈牙利和波兰这两个1956年动乱中心国家解体的新阶段开始。前者悄然开始了共产主义的一场激进经济改革；后者则以引人瞩目的方式成为第一个超越改革共产主义、对党国提出政治挑战的国家。
en: The year 1968 also marked the beginning of a new phase in the decomposition of Communism in the two East European countries that were at the center of the upheaval of 1956, Hungary and Poland. The former quietly embarked on a radical economic reform of Communism; the latter, in a spectacular way, became the first country to go beyond Reform Communism and pose a political challenge to the Party-state.

zh: 在匈牙利，经过十年镇压后，卡达尔推出了新经济机制，试图通过给予人民一点点物质繁荣来使他们与政权和解。

卡达尔的政策甚至比铁托的自我管理更大胆，是自苏联新经济政策时代以来任何共产主义政权向市场迈进得最远的一次。在农业的某些部门、小规模消费品生产以及某些服务和零售贸易领域，合作社经营得到允许，并在定价上获得相当大的自由。1970年代中期，这些半私营部门在莫斯科压力下受到约束，但在1980年代初，它们再次被允许扩张，以减少在波兰曾产生团结工会的那类不满。同样在后一时期，知识分子获得了一定程度的自由——包括出国旅行的机会——希望以此使人民接受一个无法摆脱的政权。卡达尔主义的总体结果是日益增长、尽管有限的繁荣，以及东欧最长时期的稳定——因而也是莫斯科对当地领导层的信任。然而与此同时，卡达尔低调、渐进的改革主义正在侵蚀制度的基础；没有人敢于从这一事实中得出任何大胆结论，因为每个人都吸取了1956年的可怕教训。
en: In Hungary, after a decade of repression Kadar inaugurated the New Economic Mechanism, which sought to reconcile the population with the regime by giving the former a modicum of material prosperity.

Even bolder than Tito’s self-management, Kadar’s policy was the farthest advance towards the market of any made by a Communist regime since the days of the Soviet NEP. In certain sectors of agriculture, in small-scale consumer production, and in some services and areas of retail trade, cooperative endeavors were allowed and given significant latitude in setting their prices. In the mid-1970s these semiprivate sectors were reined in under pressure from Moscow, but in the early 1980s they were again allowed to expand in order to reduce the kinds of discontent that in Poland had produced Solidarity. Also during the latter period, a measure of freedom—including the opportunity to travel abroad—was accorded to the intellectuals in the hope of reconciling the population to an unavoidable regime. The overall result of Kadarism was a growing, if modest, prosperity and the longest period of stability in Eastern Europe—and thus also the confidence of Moscow in the local leadership. At the same time, however. Kadar’s low-key, creeping reformism was eroding the foundations of the system; no one dared to draw any bold conclusions from this fact, for everyone had learned the terrible lesson of 1956.

zh: 然而在波兰，尽管这个国家摆脱控制的努力在1956年后屡遭失败，却从未有过彻底的灾难，这使人民在每次镇压后都壮起胆子重新进攻。
的确，哥穆尔卡的改革共产主义起初看来是一场胜利，最终激发了一阵社会创造力：工厂里成立了工人委员会，知识分子中出现了修正主义的“人道主义”马克思主义，科拉科夫斯基只是最著名的例子。但哥穆尔卡原来不过是一个披着民族外衣的正统共产党人：工人委员会很快被剥夺实权，知识分子日益受到骚扰。
en: In Poland, however, although the nation’s efforts to emancipate itself met with recurrent defeats after 1956, there was never an all-out disaster, and this emboldened the population after each repression to return to the attack.

Indeed, Gomulka’s Reform Communism had at first appeared as a victory, and it eventually provoked an outburst of social creativity: workers’ councils were created in the factories, and a revisionist, “humanist” Marxism emerged among the intellectuals, Kolakowski being only the most prominent example. But Gomulka turned out to be no more than an orthodox Communist with national trimmings: the workers’ councils were soon neutered and the intellectuals increasingly harassed.

zh: 哥穆尔卡新政策的第一个结果，是1968年3月政权及其警察与知识分子之间的公开冲突。这一事件带有官方反犹色彩，标志着波兰修正主义马克思主义的终结：此后，知识分子不再试图通过回归青年马克思和格奥尔格·卢卡奇来修正斯大林主义，而是将在制度轨道之外寻求一种变革哲学。哥穆尔卡回归古典共产主义风格的第二个结果，是1970年12月的格但斯克工人罢工和骚乱，莱赫·瓦文萨在此期间找到了自己的事业；像1962年的新切尔卡斯克事件一样，这些事件是由突然涨价引发的。虽然骚乱被武力镇压，工人仍然取得了某种胜利：哥穆尔卡被爱德华·盖莱克取代为党的领袖，后者不得不承诺实行照顾工人需要的政策。
en: The first result of Gomulka’s new policies was an open clash in March 1968 between the regime and its police on the one hand, and the intellectuals on the other. This episode, which was tinged with official anti-Semitism, spelled the end of revisionist Marxism in Poland: henceforth, the intellectuals would no longer try to amend Stalinism through a return to the young Marx and Gyorgy Lukacs, but would seek a philosophy of change completely outside the orbit of the system. The second result of Gomulka’s reversion to classical Communist style was the Gdansk workers’ strike and riots of December 1970, during which Lech Walesa discovered his vocation; like the events of Novocherkassk in 1962, these events were triggered by precipitate price rises. Although the riots were suppressed by force, the workers nonetheless achieved a measure of victory: Gomulka was replaced as Party leader by Edward Gierek, who had to promise a policy of catering to their needs.

zh: 因此，到1970年，知识分子和工人，当然还有教会，都已从道德上背离了制度。约70%的农民也是如此，因为波兰是共产党国家中唯一基本逃脱集体化的国家。用当时的术语说，这些群体合在一起构成了一个重新兴起的“公民社会”，公开反对“权力”。而在1970年代后半期，这个社会发展出具有政治组织雏形的团体，以及一套适合共产主义特殊条件的行动哲学。
en: Thus, as of 1970 both the intellectuals and the workers, and of course the Church, had morally defected from the system. So had some 70 percent of the peasantry, for Poland alone among Communist countries had largely escaped collectivization. Together, these groups comprised a renascent “civil society” openly opposed to the “power,” to use the terminology of the day. And in the second half of the decade this society developed a protopolitical organization and a philosophy of action suited to the special conditions of Communism.

zh: 这一发展是由盖莱克低劣版本的改革共产主义触发的。该纲领的一部分是给知识分子更大自由，包括出国旅行，这种自由只是加速了从修正主义马克思主义向西方文化多样性的转变。更重要的是，盖莱克利用缓和与东方政策，大量向西方借款，建设一个由新工业组成的“第二个波兰”，以提供安抚民众所需的消费品。但当他再也无法为这种扩张融资时，他不得不提高国内价格；这导致拉多姆和华沙乌尔苏斯工厂的罢工，他随后不得不镇压。这一事件促使一批异见知识分子为被捕罢工者创建了一个运动——工人保卫委员会，简称KOR——其最著名的人物是亚当·米赫尼克和雅采克·库龙。
en: This development was triggered by Gierek’s debased version of Reform Communism. One part of this program was a greater freedom for intellectuals, including travel abroad, a freedom that only accelerated the transition from revisionist Marxism to the cultural diversity of the West. Still more important, Gierek, profiting from détente and

, borrowed heavily from the West to build a “second Poland” of new industry that would provide the consumer goods needed to keep the population quiet. But when he could no longer pay for this expansion, he had to raise domestic prices; this led to strikes at Radom and the Ursus factory in Warsaw, which he then had to repress. This incident provoked the creation of a movement of dissident intellectuals on behalf of the arrested strikers—the Committee for Workers’ Defense, or KOR—whose most prominent figures were Adam Michnik and Jacek Kuroń.

zh: 实际上，KOR相当于知识分子和工人的具有革命雏形的联盟，因为它联合了1968年和1970年分别行动、分别失败的两支力量。然而这一次，KOR采取把问题提交政权法庭、制造社会压力的策略，迫使政权释放被捕工人。从这一成功中，KOR发展出一套适应共产主义特殊斗争条件的总体“革命”哲学：制度内改革被当作幻想放弃（捷克斯洛伐克的陷阱），而直接对抗制度则因等同自杀而受到回避（匈牙利的陷阱）。相反，KOR主张一切反对派都应采取“社会运动”或社会“自组织”的形式，以便相对于政权开辟一个自主领域。具体而言，这个领域意味着知识分子的独立学习小组“飞行大学”、萨米兹达特出版社“诺瓦”（Nowa）、几个雏形的非官方工会，当然还有教会。人们希望，用这种方法，政权会随着时间被掏空，直到不得不基本上让社会自行处理事务。
en: In effect, KOR amounted to a protorevolutionary alliance of intellectuals and workers, for it united the two forces that had moved, and been defeated, separately in 1968 and 1970. This time, however, the regime was forced to release the arrested workers through KOR’s tactic of generating social pressure by taking the matter to the regime’s courts. From this success, KOR developed a general philosophy of “revolution” adapted to the peculiar conditions of struggle under Communism: reform within the system was abandoned as an illusion (the Czechoslovak pitfall), yet direct action against the system was eschewed as suicidal (the Hungarian pitfall). Instead, KOR urged that all opposition should take the form of a “social movement,” or the “self-organization” of society, in order to stake out a sphere of autonomy vis-à-vis the regime. Concretely, this sphere meant such entities as the “flying university” of independent study groups for the intelligentsia, the

publishing house Nowa, a few embryonic unofficial trade unions, and of course the Church. By this method, it was hoped, the regime would over time be hollowed out to where it had to leave society largely to its own devices.

zh: 在波兰本身，掏空制度的过程在1978年获得巨大推动，当时波兰人约翰·保罗二世当选教皇。这一事件的影响和制度的脆弱性在次年变得明显：政权觉得拒绝约翰·保罗访问故国将是不明智的。这次访问让人民第一次发现，自己有能力动员数百万人迎接教皇。
en: In Poland itself, the process of hollowing-out the system received a great impetus in 1978 when John Paul II, a Pole, was elected pope. The impact of this event, and the fragility of the system, became apparent when the next year the regime felt it would he imprudent to refuse John Paul permission to visit his native country. The visit proved to be the first occasion when the population discovered it had the capacity to mobilize itself, and by the millions, to greet the pontiff.

zh: 这种公民社会的复兴在1980年随着团结工会的成立而公开转化为革命行动。
动荡始于格但斯克的一次新罢工，它很快采用了KOR的方法。当共产党惯用的封锁事发地点的策略未能阻止全国了解发生的事情时，罢工蔓延到其他地区，变得大到无法镇压。政权因此不得不与罢工者谈判，令他们惊讶的是，两周后政权同意承认一个有权罢工的独立工会。这是任何共产党国家第一次给予这样的承认。
en: This renascence of civil society became openly revolutionary in 1980 with the formation of Solidarity.

The upheaval began with a new strike in Gdansk that quickly took up KOR’s methods. When the usual Communist tactic of isolating the trouble spot failed to keep the country from learning what had occurred, the strike spread to other areas and became too big to be repressed. The regime therefore had to negotiate with the strikers, and to their amazement, after two weeks it agreed to recognize an independent trade union with a right to strike. This was the first time such recognition had been granted in any Communist country.

zh: 这一结果使一个本应是工人国家的政权失去了合法性。库龙有理由声称，拥有千万成员的团结工会代表了历史上最大的“无产阶级革命”，它使1917年的布尔什维克革命相形见绌——毕竟，后者的动力来自农民。然而团结工会远不止是一个工会：它体现了公民社会、实际上是整个民族为了对抗政权而自发组织起来，但其方式尚未达到与当局公开对抗的程度。因此团结工会自称是一场“自我限制的革命”。
en: This outcome delegitimized what was supposed to be a workers’ state. Kuron was right to claim that Solidarity, with its ten million members, represented the largest “proletarian revolution” in history, one that quite dwarfed the Bolshevik Revolution of 1917, whose motive force, after all, had been the peasantry. Yet Solidarity was much more than a trade union: it represented the self-organization of civil society, indeed of the nation, against the regime, but in a manner that fell short of open confrontation with the authorities. Solidarity therefore referred to itself as a “self-limiting revolution.”

zh: 具体而言，团结工会逐渐要求波兰的“芬兰化”和一个“自治共和国”。这意味着苏联将保留对波兰军事和外交政策的控制，而社会将管理其主要内部事务，让党只居于统而不治的地位，像英国女王一样。然而实际上，这位红色女王将保留相当多的权力：尽管团结工会想要独立工会和市场经济，其1981年10月的纲领却不敢主张国有工业私有化，因为这会过于吓坏苏联人。因此，团结工会远远超越了改革共产主义，但仍不得不满足于某种中途方案。
en: Specifically, Solidarity came to demand the “Finlandization” of Poland and a “self-governing republic.” This meant that the Soviets would retain control of Poland’s military and foreign policy while society would manage its principal internal affairs, leaving the Party only to reign but not rule, like the Queen of England. In fact, however, this Red queen would retain quite a bit of power: although Solidarity wanted independent trade unions and a market-oriented economy, its Program of October 1981 did not dare advocate the privatization of state industry, for this would have frightened the Soviets too much. Hence, Solidarity went well beyond Reform Communism but was still obliged to settle for something of a halfway house.

zh: 然而，认为团结工会有什么固定目标将是错误的。它的存在就是一场漫长的赌博：起初，这个组织只是为了生存而拖延时间；后来，它在继续生存的同时争取扩大允许活动的界限。因为它从未幻想党已接受它存在的权利，也从未幻想“伙伴关系”政策对任何一方来说不只是策略。它反复高呼的座右铭是：“我们所做的事情是不可能的，同时又是必要的。”于是，团结工会成员故意对明显的危险视而不见，把这场存在性赌博坚持了这前所未有的十六个月，希望如果他们能坚持足够久，对手也许真的会接受权力分享。尽管他们的赌博没有以这种方式得到回报，却仍然带来了巨大收益：到不可避免的镇压来临时，团结工会已经把波兰的共产主义制度掏空到无法修复的地步。而这一壮举，而非任何具体的社会成果，才是团结工会的主要和原创成就。
en: Yet it would be a mistake to think that Solidarity had fixed goals of any kind. Its existence was one long gamble: At the beginning, the organization played for time simply in order to exist; later, it played to expand the limits of the permissible and yet continue to exist. For it never had any illusions that the Party had accepted its right to be there, or that a policy of “partnership” was anything more than a tactic for either side. Its oft-repeated motto was, “What we are doing is impossible and at the same time necessary.” So the members of Solidarity, deliberately closing their eyes to the obvious dangers, kept this existential wager going for sixteen unprecedented months in the hope that if they could hold out long enough, their adversary might actually accept power sharing. Although their gamble did not pay off in this way, it did yield a great return nonetheless: by the time the inevitable crackdown came, Solidarity had hollowed out Poland’s Communist system beyond any possibility of repair. And this feat, rather than any particular social conquest, was Solidarity’s major and original achievement.

zh: 在取得这一结果的过程中，波兰人无意中得到了苏联人异常犹豫不决的帮助。起初，在1980年8月，团结工会爆发的突然性和运动的规模排除了华沙或莫斯科进行武装镇压的可能：尽管双方都不打算永久容忍团结工会，他们也别无选择，只能拖延时间。苏联人先在12月动员准备干预，但随后退缩。1981年2月，他们预期的卡达尔、国防部长沃伊切赫·雅鲁泽尔斯基将军被授予第一书记的额外头衔，有条不紊的镇压准备工作开始了。苏联人最后似乎在3月准备干预，然后在9月又一次准备，但事情仍然没有超出神经战。作为实际进攻的前奏，10月雅鲁泽尔斯基成为总理，同时保留此前所有头衔。
en: In arriving at this result the Poles were inadvertently aided by the exceptional indecisiveness of the Soviets. At the beginning, in August 1980, the suddenness of Solidarity’s eruption and the size of the movement ruled out armed repression by either Warsaw or Moscow: Although neither had any intention of tolerating Solidarity permanently, they also had no choice but to play for time. The Soviets first mobilized for intervention in December but then backed off. In February 1981 their presumptive Kadar, the minister of defense, General Wojciech Jaruzelski, was given the additional title of First Secretary, and methodical preparations for a crackdown were begun. The Soviets at last seemed ready to intervene in March, and then once more in September, but still matters did not go beyond a war of nerves. As a prelude to the actual assault, in October Jaruzelski became prime minister while keeping all of his previous titles.

children: 〔译注〕原书颠倒了任职时间：雅鲁泽尔斯基1981年2月出任总理，10月出任党第一书记，并继续兼任国防部长。
〔译注〕原书颠倒了任职时间：雅鲁泽尔斯基1981年2月出任总理，10月出任党第一书记，并继续兼任国防部长。

zh: 为什么事情拖了这么久，仍不清楚。也许国家的规模——以及团结工会的规模——使这次行动比在匈牙利或捷克斯洛伐克的情况要艰巨得多。另一个可能的原因是苏联人此时已陷在阿富汗。无论如何，只是在经过大量辩论后，雅鲁泽尔斯基和苏联人才最终一致认为，对两个政权来说代价最小的做法是由波兰军队单独实施“戒严状态”。于是，1981年12月13日，这场自我占领以这一体制在经济领域从未表现出的效率实施了。
en: Why matters dragged on for this long a time is still not clear. Perhaps the size of the country—and of Solidarity—made the operation much more daunting than had been the case in Hungary or Czechoslovakia. Possibly another reason was that the Soviets were now bogged down in Afghanistan. In any event, it was only after much debate that Jaruzelski and the Soviets finally agreed that the least costly course for the two regimes would be a “state of siege” imposed by Polish forces alone. So on December 13, 1981, this self-occupation was carried out with an efficiency the system had never displayed with the economy.

zh: 表面上看，这一结果像是匈牙利和捷克斯洛伐克结局的重演，当时几乎所有西方观察家都这样宣称；然而实际上，结果却远没有那样一锤定音。莫斯科犹豫了——而团结工会幸存了——十六个月，这一事实表明制度实际上可以被击退。进一步的事实是，在摊牌时刻，莫斯科第一次不敢亲自下手，这也表明活力丧失。整个东欧都注意到了这一切。
en: On the surface, this outcome looked like a replay of the Hungarian and Czechoslovak denouements, as almost all Western observers declared at the time; in reality, however, the result was far less decisive. The fact that Moscow had hesitated—and Solidarity had survived—for sixteen months demonstrated that the system could in fact be rolled back. The further fact that at the moment of showdown Moscow, for the first time, had not dared to do the deed itself also indicated a loss of vitality. And all of this was noted throughout Eastern Europe.

zh: 此外，波兰并没有被“正常化”：雅鲁泽尔斯基确实想成为他那个十年的卡达尔，但他只维持了一年镇压，随后就进入行动的第二阶段，即新的改革共产主义。与此同时，团结工会虽然被迫转入地下，却在整个八十年代仍然很有活力；它不把雅鲁泽尔斯基的改革视为解决办法，而视为有朝一日实现“正常社会”的前奏。因此，团结工会的第一阶段（1980—1981）不是以灾难告终，而只是以挫折告终，就像1956年以来波兰与制度的所有其他交锋一样。而这一结果将为1989年的大结局提供基础。
en: Poland, moreover, was not “normalized”: Jaruzelski, who indeed wanted to be the Kadar of his decade, kept up repression for only a year and then moved to the second phase of his operation, a new Reform Communism. At the same time, Solidarity, though driven underground, remained very much alive throughout the eighties; and it viewed Jaruzelski’s reforms not as a solution but as a prelude to someday achieving a “normal society.” Thus the first phase of Solidarity, in 1980-1981, ended not in a disaster but only in a setback, like all the other Polish brushes with the system since 1956. And this outcome would provide the basis for the grand denouement of 1989.

zh: 到1982年勃列日涅夫去世时，苏联在东欧的外部帝国的账目明显是负的。苏联武装力量或其代理人不得不在柏林、布达佩斯、布拉格和华沙镇压“反革命”。虽然这些干预在西方看来具有侵略性和威胁性，实际上却是防御性的、保守的努力，尽管代价高昂，目的是保住第二次世界大战的成果。与此同时，南斯拉夫和罗马尼亚已退出阵营。华沙条约远非苏联安全的附属品或抵御无人考虑的攻击的盾牌，反而成了苏联制度的又一个负担。
en: By Brezhnev’s death in 1982, the balance sheet of the Soviet External Empire in Eastern Europe was palpably negative. Soviet armed forces or their proxies had been obliged to suppress “counterrevolution” in Berlin, Budapest, Prague, and Warsaw. Although these interventions had appeared aggressive and threatening to the West, they were in fact defensive and conservative, albeit costly, efforts to hold on to the gains of the Second World War. At the same time, Yugoslavia and Romania had seceded from the bloc. The Warsaw Pact, far from being an adjunct to Soviet security or a shield against an attack that no one was contemplating, had become still another burden on the Soviet system.

zh: 此外，东欧各国的经济停滞得几乎和苏联经济一样严重，而且都远远落后于日益繁荣的（西）欧洲共同体。最后，尽管有镇压，整个地区都在软化，无论是通过匈牙利和波兰的政权政策，还是通过西德和奥地利电视节目对东德和捷克斯洛伐克产生的影响。经过近四十年的社会主义，当地民众不再幻想制度能给他们一个真正的未来。他们知道自己只是被囚禁的民族；而制度本质上靠1945年以来积累的恐惧资本维持。但有了团结工会，连这种恐惧也开始消退。当下一次改革共产主义的努力失控时，莫斯科是否有能力干预，此时已是一个悬而未决的问题。
en: The economies of Eastern Europe, moreover, were stagnating almost as badly as the economy of the Soviet Union, and all were far behind the increasingly prosperous (West) European Community. Finally, despite the repression, the entire region was softening up, whether through regime policy in Hungary and Poland or via the reach of West German and Austrian television in East Germany and Czechoslovakia. After almost four decades of socialism, there was no longer any illusion among the local populations that the system offered them a genuine future. They knew they were simply captive nations; and the system lived essentially off the capital of fear accumulated since 1945. But with Solidarity, even this fear had begun to ebb. It was now an open question whether Moscow would have the capacity to intervene the next time an effort at Reform Communism spun out of control.

zh: 尽管如此，苏联的任何外部问题——从团结工会到阿富汗——除非先在国内发生危机，否则都无法撼动制度。而在1980年代初的苏联，存在众多潜在的危机因素——从经济停滞到党的硬化到地缘政治过度扩张。然而，如果没有一个促发性的冲击，这些因素都不可能公开浮现或凝结为总体危机。而这种冲击只能来自最高层，因为制度的结构决定了一切主动行动都必须来自上面。的确，苏联政策的每一次转变——从战时共产主义到新经济政策，再到赫鲁晓夫的去斯大林化——都是以自上而下的革命方式发生的。
en: Still, none of the Soviet Union’s external problems—from Solidarity to Afghanistan—would be capable of shaking the system unless there were first a crisis at home. And there were numerous latent elements of crisis in the Soviet Union at the start of the 1980s—from the stagnation of the economy to the sclerosis of the Party to geopolitical overextension. Yet none of these elements could emerge into the open or congeal into general crisis without a precipitating shock. And this shock could originate only at the top, for the structure of the system was such that all initiative had to come from on high. Indeed, every shift of Soviet policy—from War Communism to the NEP to Khrushchev’s de-Stalinization—had come as a revolution from above.

zh: 然而，勃列日涅夫一代——斯大林在1930年代末通过清洗进行社会晋升的最后果实——随着年迈衰弱完全无力采取任何此类主动。因此，在保卫社会主义在阿富汗和波兰的成果的努力之后，它只是滑入进一步衰退。由于制度如此集中，在这些年迈的统治者相继去世之前，这种困境无路可走。这种情况导致了一个三年过渡期，在此期间，他们一个接一个地被安葬在克里姆林宫墙边。而这个阴森的过程就是危机的最后因素，它产生了改革共产主义的终极形态——戈尔巴乔夫的改革。
en: However, the Brezhnev generation—the final fruit of Stalin’s social promotion through purge at the end of the 1930s—in its geriatric decline was quite incapable of any such initiative. Hence, after the exertions of defending the conquests of socialism in Afghanistan and Poland, it simply coasted into further decline. Because the system was so centralized, there would be no way out of this predicament until the gerontocrats had physically passed from the scene.
